body.translated_text: Now, therefore, [there is] an inquiry into <s>dharma</s> for the purpose of the supreme good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>) of man.
And one who, having known [it], follows [it], is righteous (<s>dhārmika</s>).

body.text: Va.1.3 praśasya(pra-śaṃs-).tamas^bhavati(bhū-) loke pretya(pra-i-) ca svarga.lokam^samaśnute(sam-aś-) //
body.translated_text: He becomes the most praiseworthy in the world, and after death attains the heavenly world.
<s>Dharma</s> is that which is ordained by <s>śruti</s> (revealed scripture) and <s>smṛti</s> (remembered tradition).
In the absence of these, the conduct of the learned (<s>śiṣṭa</s>) is authoritative.
A learned person (<s>śiṣṭa</s>), moreover, is one who is free from selfish desire.
<s>Dharma</s> is that whose cause cannot be grasped [by reason alone].

body.text: Va.1.8 ārya.āvartas^prāk^ādarśāt pratyak kālakavanāt^udak pāriyātrāt^dakṣiṇena himavatas^//
body.translated_text: <s>Āryāvarta</s> (the land of the noble) [is the region] east of <s>Ādarśa</s>, west of <s>Kālakavana</s>, north of <s>Pāriyātra</s>, and south of the <s>Himālayas</s>.
And north of the <s>Vindhya</s> [mountains].

body.text: Va.1.10 tasmin deśe ye dharmās ye ca^ācārās te sarvatra pratyetavyās(prati-i-)^//
body.translated_text: The <s>dharmas</s> and customs that exist in that region are to be accepted everywhere.
But not those of others who follow contrary practices.
Some [say it is] the region between the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and <s>Yamunā</s>.
Others [say] it extends as far as the black antelope roams — [there is] the splendor of <s>Brahman</s>.
Moreover, in the <s>Nidāna</s> of the <s>Bhāllavins</s>, they cite a verse:
Behind [is] the <s>Sindhu</s> (Indus), the divider; before [is] the rising of the sun;

body.text: Va.1.15 yāvat kṛṣṇas^abhidhāvati(abhi-dhāv-) tāvat^vai brahma.varcasam iti //
body.translated_text: As far as the black [antelope] runs, so far indeed [extends] the splendor of <s>Brahman</s>.
What the elders versed in the three <s>Vedas</s>, the knowers of <s>dharma</s>, declare to be <s>dharma</s>,

body.text: Va.1.16 pavane pāvane ca^eva sa dharmas^na^atra saṃśayas.(c) iti //
body.translated_text: That which is purifying and pure — that is <s>dharma</s>; there is no doubt about this.
<s>Manu</s> declared the <s>dharmas</s> of region, the <s>dharmas</s> of caste, and the <s>dharmas</s> of family [to be authoritative] in the absence of <s>śruti</s>.

One who sleeps at sunrise, one who sleeps at sunset, one with deformed nails, one with discolored teeth, one whose younger brother marries first, one who marries before his elder brother, one who gives a daughter to such a person, the husband of such a woman, a slayer of a hero, and one who abandons the <s>Veda</s> — these are sinners (<s>enasvin</s>).
They declare five great sins (<s>mahāpātaka</s>).
Violation of the teacher's bed, drinking of <s>surā</s> (liquor), killing of an embryo [or a learned <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>], stealing of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>'s gold, and association with a fallen person.
[Association] either through sacred rites (<s>brāhma</s>) or through blood relation (<s>yauna</s>).
Moreover, they cite:
One who associates with a fallen person falls [from caste] within a year,
Through sacrificing for him, teaching him, and [sharing] blood relation — but not through traveling together, sitting together, or giving.

One who discards the sacred fires, one who strikes one's teacher, an atheist (<s>nāstika</s>), one who follows the conduct of an atheist, and one who sells <s>soma</s> — these are secondary sins (<s>upapātaka</s>).

body.text: Va.1.24 tisras^brāhmaṇasya bhāryās^varṇa.anupūrveṇa dve rājanyasya ekaikā vaiśya.śūdrayos^//
body.translated_text: A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> may have three wives in accordance with the order of <s>varṇas</s>, a <s>Kṣatriya</s> two, and a <s>Vaiśya</s> and <s>Śūdra</s> one each.
Some [permit] even a <s>Śūdra</s> [wife for a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>], but without [Vedic] <s>mantras</s>, in the same manner.
One should not do so.
For from this there certainly follows the degradation of the family, and after death, the loss of heaven.
There are six [forms of] marriage.
The <s>Brāhma</s>, <s>Daiva</s>, <s>Ārṣa</s>, <s>Gāndharva</s>, <s>Kṣātra</s>, and <s>Mānuṣa</s>.
When one gives [a daughter] to a man of one's choice with a [preceding] water [offering], that is the <s>Brāhma</s> [marriage].

body.text: Va.1.31 yajña.tantre vitate(vi-tan-)^ṛtvije karma kurvate(kṛ-) kanyām^dadyāt(dā-)^alaṃkṛtya(alam-kṛ-) tam^daivam iti^ācakṣate(ā-cakṣ-) //
body.translated_text: When one gives an adorned maiden to a <s>ṛtvij</s> (officiating priest) while a sacrifice is being performed, they call that the <s>Daiva</s> [marriage].
And with [the gift of] a pair of cattle, [it is] the <s>Ārṣa</s>.
When one, desiring [her], marries a willing [maiden] of equal birth, that is the <s>Gāndharva</s>.

body.text: Va.1.34 yām^[balena sahasā pramathya(pra-math-)] haranti(hṛ-) sa kṣātras^//
body.translated_text: When they carry away [a maiden] by force, overpowering [her], that is the <s>Kṣātra</s>.
When [a maiden is] purchased for a price after bargaining, that is the <s>Mānuṣa</s>.
Therefore, [the rule that] a hundred [coins] upon a chariot are to be given to the father of the bride — this is understood here as a purchase.

body.text: Va.1.37 yā patyus^krītā satī^atha^anyais^carati(car-)^iti ha cāturmāsyeṣu //
body.translated_text: In the <s>Cāturmāsya</s> [sacrifices, it is said]: 'She who, having been purchased by her husband, then goes with others.'
Moreover, they cite:

body.text: Va.1.38 vidyā pranaṣṭā punar abhyupaiti(abhi-upa-i-) kula.praṇāśe tu^iha sarva.nāśas^(c)/
body.translated_text: Lost learning can be recovered, but when a family is destroyed, there is total destruction;

body.text: Va.1.38 kula.apadeśena hayas^api pūjyas tasmāt kulīnām^striyam udvahanti(ud-vah-).(c) iti //
body.translated_text: By the name of one's family, even a horse is honored; therefore, they marry a woman of good family.
The three <s>varṇas</s> should live under the direction of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.
The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should declare the <s>dharmas</s>.
And the king should enforce [them].

body.text: Va.1.42 rājā tu dharmeṇa^anuśāsan(anu-śās-) ṣaṣṭham^dhanasya haret(hṛ-) //
body.translated_text: The king, governing justly, should take one-sixth of [the people's] wealth.
Except from <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>.

body.text: Va.1.44 iṣṭāpūrtasya tu ṣaṣṭham aṃśam^bhajati(bhaj-)^iti ha //
body.translated_text: But he receives a sixth share of the [merit of] <s>iṣṭāpūrta</s> (sacrificial and charitable works), so it is said.

body.text: Va.1.45 brāhmaṇas^vedam āḍhyam^karoti(kṛ-) brāhmaṇo āpadas^uddharati(ud-hṛ-) tasmāt^brāhmaṇas^anādyas^/ somas^asya rājā bhavati(bhū-)^iti ha //
body.translated_text: The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> enriches the <s>Veda</s>; the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> rescues from calamities; therefore, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is not to be consumed; <s>Soma</s> is his king — so it is said.

body.text: Va.1.46 pretya(pra-i-) ca^ābhyudayikam iti ha vijñāyate(vi-jñā-) ha vijñāyate(vi-jñā-)^iti //
body.translated_text: And after death, [there is] prosperity — so it is known, so it is known.
There are four <s>varṇas</s>: <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>Kṣatriya</s>, <s>Vaiśya</s>, and <s>Śūdra</s>.
Three <s>varṇas</s> are twice-born (<s>dvijāti</s>): <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>Kṣatriya</s>, and <s>Vaiśya</s>.
Of these,
The first birth is from the mother; the second at the tying of the <s>muñja</s> girdle;

body.text: Va.2.3 atra^asya mātā sāvitrī pitā tu^ācāryas^ucyate(vac-) (c)//
body.translated_text: Here, the <s>Sāvitrī</s> [verse] is said to be his mother, and the teacher (<s>ācārya</s>) his father.
Because of giving the <s>Veda</s>, they call the teacher 'father.'
Moreover, they cite:

body.text:
Va.2.5 dvayam u ha vai puruṣasya retas^brāhmaṇasya^ūrdhvam^nābhes^adhastāt^avācīnam anyat tat^yat^ūrdhvam^nābhes tena ha^etat prajā jāyate(jan-) yat^brāhmaṇān upanayati(upa-nī-) yat^adhyāpayati(adhi-i-) yat^yājayati(yaj-) yat sādhukaroti(sādhu-kṛ-) / atha yat^avācīnam^nābhes tena^iha^asya^aurasī prajā jāyate(jan-) / tasmāt^śrotriyam anūcānam a.prajas^asi(as-)^iti
na vadanti(vad-)^iti //
body.translated_text: Indeed, a man's — a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>'s — seed is twofold: that which is above the navel and that which is below. That which is above the navel — by that, offspring is produced when he initiates <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, when he teaches them, when he officiates at sacrifices for them, and when he does good deeds. And that which is below the navel — by that, his bodily offspring is produced here. Therefore, they do not say of a learned man versed in tradition that he is 'without offspring.'
<s>Hārīta</s> also cites:

body.text: Va.2.6 na hi^asmin vidyate(vid-) karma kim.cit^ā mauñji.bandhanāt (c)/
body.translated_text: Indeed, no sacred rite exists for him before the tying of the <s>muñja</s> girdle;

body.text: Va.2.6 vṛttyā śūdra.samas^hi^eṣa yāvat^vede na jāyate(jan-).(c) iti //
body.translated_text: In conduct, he is equal to a <s>Śūdra</s> until he is born in the <s>Veda</s>.
Except for [rites] connected with water, ritual actions, the <s>svadhā</s> offering, and the ancestors.

body.text: Va.2.8 vidyā ha vai brāhmaṇam ājagāma(gam-) gopāya mām^śevadhis te^aham asmi(as-) (c)/
body.translated_text: Learning indeed came to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [and said]: 'Protect me! I am your treasure.'

body.text: Va.2.8 asūyakāya^an.ṛjave^a.yatāya na mām^brūyās(brū-)^vīryavatī tathā syām(as-) (c)//
body.translated_text: 'Do not impart me to one who is envious, crooked, or undisciplined — thus shall I be powerful.'
'To the one whom you know to be pure, attentive, intelligent, and endowed with <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate studentship),'

body.text: Va.2.9 yas te na druhyet(druh-) katamat.cana^ahar^tasmai mām^brūyās(brū-)^nidhipāya brahman (c)//
body.translated_text: 'Who would never betray you on any day — to him impart me as a treasure, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.'
He who fills the ears with what is true, causing no pain and bestowing immortality,

body.text: Va.2.10 tam^manyeta(man-) pitaram^mātaram^ca tasmai na druhyet(druh-) katamaccana^ahar^(c)//
body.translated_text: Him one should regard as father and mother; one should never betray him on any day.

body.text: Va.2.11 adhyāpitās^ye gurum^na^ādriyante(ā-dṛ-) viprās^vācā manasā karmaṇā vā (c)/
body.translated_text: Those <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who, having been taught, do not honor the teacher by word, mind, or deed,

body.text: Va.2.11 yathā^eva te na guros^bhojanīyās(bhuj-) tathā^eva tān na bhunakti(bhuj-) śrutam^tat (c)//
body.translated_text: Just as they are not worthy of the teacher's food, so too that sacred learning does not nourish them.
As fire burns dry grass, so the <s>Veda</s>, when asked of but not respected,

body.text: Va.2.12 na brahma tasmai prabrūyāt(pra-brū-)^śakyam^mānam akurvata(kṛ-)(c) iti //
body.translated_text: [Burns the student]. One should not teach the <s>Veda</s> to one who is capable but does not show respect.
Six are the duties of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.
Studying [the <s>Veda</s>] through self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>), teaching, performing sacrifice, officiating at sacrifice, giving gifts, and accepting gifts.
Three are [the duties] of a <s>Kṣatriya</s>.
Studying, performing sacrifice, and giving gifts.

body.text: Va.2.17 śastreṇa ca prajā.pālanam^sva.dharmas tena jīvet(jīv-) //
body.translated_text: And protecting the people by means of arms — by that, his own <s>dharma</s>, he should live.
These same [three duties belong] to a <s>Vaiśya</s>.
[Additionally:] agriculture, trade, cattle-rearing, and lending at interest.

body.text: Va.2.20 teṣām^paricaryā śūdrasya niyatā ca vṛttis^//
body.translated_text: Service to those [three <s>varṇas</s>] is the <s>Śūdra</s>'s [duty], and a fixed livelihood.
All [should wear] their hair in a regulated style, or [keep it] loose except for the topknot (<s>śikhā</s>).
Those unable to live by their own <s>dharma</s> may adopt the livelihood of the next lower [<s>varṇa</s>].
But never [the livelihood] of a higher one.
When adopting a <s>Vaiśya</s>'s livelihood and living by trade, [the following may not be traded:] rock-salt, gems, hemp, silk, linen, and hides.
And all [cloth] that is woven and dyed.

body.text: Va.2.26 kṛta.annam^puṣpa.phala.mūlāni gandha.rasās^udakam^ca^oṣadhīnām^rasas^somas^ca śastram^viṣam^māṃsam^ca kṣīram^ca sa.vikāram ayas trapu jatu sīsam^ca //
body.translated_text: [Also not to be traded:] prepared food; flowers, fruits, and roots; perfumes and flavors; water; the juice of plants; <s>soma</s>; weapons; poison; meat; milk and its products; iron, tin, lac, and lead.
Moreover, they cite:

body.text: Va.2.27 sadyas^patati(pat-) māṃsena lākṣayā lavaṇena ca (c)/
body.translated_text: One falls [from caste] immediately by [trading in] meat, lac, and salt;
Within three days, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> becomes [equal to] a <s>Śūdra</s> by selling milk.

body.text: Va.2.28 grāma.paśūnām eka.śaphās^keśinas^ca sarve ca^āraṇyās^paśavas^vayāṃsi daṃṣṭriṇas^ca //
body.translated_text: [Also not to be traded:] among domestic animals, those with undivided hooves and those with manes; and all wild animals, birds, and those with fangs.
Among grains, they say [one should not trade] sesame.
Moreover, they cite:
Whatever one does with sesame other than eating, anointing, and giving,
One sinks, becoming a worm in dog's excrement, together with one's ancestors.
Or, if one wishes, one may sell sesame that one has plowed and produced oneself.

body.text: Va.2.32 tasmāt^sāṇḍābhyām a.nasi.otābhyām^prāk prātar.āśāt karṣī syāt(as-) //
body.translated_text: Therefore, one should plow before the morning meal with two [bulls] that are uncastrated and not pierced in the nose.
In summer, one should offer water [to travelers].
[The plowshare hymn:] 'The plow, having a good share, auspicious, <s>Soma</s>-sipped —'

body.text: Va.2.34 tad ud vapati(vap-) gām avim^prapharvyam^ca pīvarīm^prasthāvat^ratha.vāhanam iti //
body.translated_text: 'It scatters forth a cow, a sheep, a well-nourished plump [woman], and a chariot with draft-animal.'

body.text: (2.35) lāṅgalam^pavīravat^vīravat sumanuṣyavat^anaḍudvat su.śevam^kalyāṇa.nāsikam^kalyāṇī hi^asya nāsikā nāsikathā^udvapati(ud-vap-) dūre^apavidhyati(apa-vyadh-) soma.pitsaru somas^hi^asya prāpnoti(pra-āp-) tat saru tat^udvapati(ud-vap-) gām^ca^avim^ca^ajān aśvān aśvatara.kharoṣṭān^ca prapharvyam^ca pīvarīm^darśanīyām^kalyāṇīm^ca prathama.yuvatīm //
body.translated_text: Variant: 'The plow, having a good share, having heroes, having good men, having bullocks, auspicious, having a good plowshare — for its plowshare is good — by means of the plowshare it scatters forth, it throws far; <s>Soma</s>-sipped — for <s>Soma</s> reaches it, that is the essence, that it scatters forth: a cow, a sheep, goats, horses, mules and camels, and a well-nourished, plump, fair, and lovely young woman.'
How, indeed, could the plow scatter [all this] except through the sale of grain?
Flavors may be exchanged for flavors, either of greater or lesser [value].
But salt [may] not [be exchanged] for flavors.

body.text: Va.2.39 tila.taṇḍula.pakvānam^vidyā mānuṣyās^ca vihitās^parivarttakena //{BṣPṣ parivarttakena}{F parivartakena}
body.translated_text: The exchange of sesame, rice, and cooked food, as well as human [labor], is prescribed by way of barter.
A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and a <s>Kṣatriya</s> should not lend at interest.
Moreover, they cite:
One who, having taken out grain at the [current] price, gives [it back later] at a higher price,

body.text: Va.2.41 sa vai vārdhuṣikas^nāma brahma.vādiṣu garhitas^(c)//
body.translated_text: He indeed is called a usurer (<s>vārdhuṣika</s>) and is condemned among those who follow the <s>Veda</s>.
(Va.2.42) He weighed the slaying of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and interest on a balance;
(Va.2.42) The slayer of an embryo stood at the tip [of the balance], and the usurer trembled. Thus [ends the citation].
(Va.2.43) Or one may give [the loan at interest] willingly to one whose [means of] livelihood have been lost, [even] to a wicked person.
(Va.2.44) Double [the rate] for gold, triple for grain.
(Va.2.45) By grain alone are the rates for liquids explained.
(Va.2.46) And for flowers, roots, and fruits.
(Va.2.47) [The interest on] what is held in the balance [i.e., weighed commodities] is eightfold.
(Va.2.48) And moreover they cite:
(Va.2.48) Two, three, four, and five percent are prescribed
(Va.2.48) As the monthly interest to be taken for the [four] <s>varṇas</s> (castes) in order.
(Va.2.49) A king should destroy [excessive] interest on capital by [assuming] the attitude of the dead [i.e., a moratorium];
(Va.2.49) And by a fresh royal consecration, the capital increases again.
(Va.2.50) Hear the interest declared by the words of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> regarding usury:

body.text: Va.2.50 pañca māṣās tu viṃśatyā evam^dharmas^na hīyate(hā-).(c) iti //
body.translated_text: (Va.2.50) Five <s>māṣas</s> on twenty — thus <s>dharma</s> is not violated. Thus [ends the citation].
(Va.2.50) 'Is not violated' — thus.

(Va.3.1) Non-<s>śrotriyas</s> (those who have not studied the Veda), those for whom the <s>anuvākyā</s> (invocatory verses) are not recited, and those without [sacred] fires — they become equal to <s>Śūdras</s> in their observances.
(Va.3.2) And here they cite a verse from <s>Manu</s>:

body.text: Va.3.2 yas^anadhītya(adhi-i-) dvijas^vedam anyatra kurute(kṛ-) śramam (c)/
body.translated_text: (Va.3.2) A twice-born who, without having studied the <s>Veda</s>, exerts himself in another [pursuit],

body.text: Va.3.2 sa jīvan(jīv-)^eva śūdratvam āśu gacchati(gam-) sa.anvayas^(c)//
body.translated_text: (Va.3.2) While still living, quickly reaches the status of a <s>Śūdra</s>, together with his lineage.
(Va.3.3) He is no <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who has not [studied] the <s>Ṛc</s> [Veda], nor a merchant, nor a performer (<s>kuśīlava</s>),

body.text: Va.3.3 na śūdra.preṣaṇam^kurvan(kṛ-) na stenas^na cikitsakas^(c)//
body.translated_text: (Va.3.3) Nor one who does the bidding of a <s>Śūdra</s>, nor a thief, nor a physician.
(Va.3.4) Where twice-born men who are without vows and without study wander about as begging mendicants,
(Va.3.4) The king should punish that village, for it is [tantamount to] providing food for thieves.
(Va.3.5) Of those without vows and without sacred mantras, who subsist merely on their birth [as Brahmins],
(Va.3.5) Even [if] assembled in thousands, there is no [authority of an] assembly.
(Va.3.6) What those who are enveloped in darkness, fools ignorant of <s>dharma</s>, declare —
(Va.3.6) That sin, having become a hundredfold, overtakes those who spoke it.
(Va.3.7) What three or even four who have mastered the <s>Veda</s> declare —
(Va.3.7) That is to be known as <s>dharma</s>, not [the declaration] of thousands of others.

body.text: Va.3.8 śrotriyāya ca deyāni havya.kavyāni nityaśas^(c)/
body.translated_text: (Va.3.8) Oblations to the gods (<s>havya</s>) and offerings to the ancestors (<s>kavya</s>) should always be given to a <s>śrotriya</s> (learned Brahmin);

body.text: Va.3.8 a.śrotriyāya dattam^hi pitṝn na^eti(i-) na devatās^(c)//
body.translated_text: (Va.3.8) For what is given to one who is not a <s>śrotriya</s> reaches neither the ancestors nor the gods.

body.text: Va.3.9 yasya ca^eka.gṛhe mūrkhas^dūre vā^api bahu.śrutas^(c)/
body.translated_text: (Va.3.9) And even if an ignorant person is in one's own household and a learned man (<s>bahuśruta</s>) is far away,
(Va.3.9) One should give to the learned man; there is no transgression [in passing over] the ignorant.
(Va.3.10) There is no offense against a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> in [passing over] a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> devoid of Vedic [learning];

body.text: Va.3.10 jvalantam agnim utsṛjya(ud-sṛj-) na hi bhasmani hūyate(hu-) (c)//
body.translated_text: (Va.3.10) For, having left aside a blazing fire, one does not sacrifice into ashes.
(Va.3.11) A wooden elephant, a leather deer,

body.text: Va.3.11 yas^ca vipras^anadhīyānas trayas te nāma.dhārakās^(c)//
body.translated_text: (Va.3.11) And a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> without Vedic study — these three are name-bearers [only].
(Va.3.12) In those kingdoms where ignorant men eat what should be [eaten by] the learned,

body.text: Va.3.12 tāni^an.āvṛṣṭim ṛcchanti(ṛ-) mahat^vā jāyate(jan-) bhayam(c) iti //
body.translated_text: (Va.3.12) Those [kingdoms] suffer drought, or great calamity arises. Thus [ends the citation].
(Va.3.13) Ownerless wealth that is unrecognized — the king may take it, giving a sixth share to the finder.

body.text: Va.3.14 brāhmaṇas^cet^adhigacchet(adhi-gam-) ṣaṭsu karmasu varttamānas(vṛt-)^na rājā haret(hṛ-) //{BṣPṣ varttamānas}{F vartamānas}
body.translated_text: (Va.3.14) But if a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> engaged in the six [prescribed] activities finds it, the king should not take it.

body.text: Va.3.15 ātatāyinam^hatvā(han-) na^atra prāṇa.chettus^kim.cit kilviṣam āhur(ah-)^//
body.translated_text: (Va.3.15) Having killed an assailant (<s>ātatāyin</s>), they declare that there is no guilt whatsoever for the killer.
(Va.3.16) And moreover they cite:
(Va.3.16) An arsonist, a poisoner, one with weapon in hand, a robber of wealth,
(Va.3.16) And a seizer of fields and wives — these six are [called] assailants (<s>ātatāyins</s>).
(Va.3.17) An approaching assailant, even if he has mastered the <s>Vedānta</s>,
(Va.3.17) One who intends to kill may be killed — by that [act] one does not become a slayer of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.
(Va.3.18) One who kills an assailant who is devoted to Vedic study and born in a [good] family —

body.text: Va.3.18 na tena bhrūṇahā sa syāt(as-)^manyus tat.manyum ṛcchati(ṛ-).(c) iti //
body.translated_text: (Va.3.18) By that [act] he would not be a slayer of an embryo; [for] anger encounters anger. Thus [ends the citation].

body.text: Va.3.19 triṇāciketas^pañca.agnis tri.suparṇas^catus.medhā vājasaneyī ṣaṭ.aṅga.vid^brahma.deya.anusantānas^chandogas^jyeṣṭha.sāma.gas^mantra.brāhmaṇa.vidyas^ca dharmān adhīte(adhi-i-) yasya ca daśa.puruṣam^mātṛ.pitṛ.vaṃśas^śrotriyas^vijñāyate(vi-jñā-) vidvāṃsas^snātakās^ca^ete paṅkti.pāvanās^bhavanti(bhū-) //
body.translated_text: (Va.3.19) One who has performed the <s>Triṇāciketa</s> [fire rite], one who maintains the five fires, one who knows the <s>Trisuparṇa</s>, one who has performed the four great sacrifices (<s>caturmedhā</s>), a follower of the <s>Vājasaneya</s> [school], one who knows the six <s>Vedāṅgas</s>, one whose lineage has been consecrated through [the giving of] <s>brahmadeya</s> gifts, a <s>Chandoga</s> (Sāma Veda scholar), one who chants the <s>Jyeṣṭha Sāman</s>, one who knows both the <s>Mantras</s> and the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, one who studies the <s>dharmas</s>, and one whose lineage on both the maternal and paternal sides is known to have been learned (<s>śrotriya</s>) for ten generations — these learned ones and <s>snātakas</s> (graduated students) are purifiers of the row [of diners at a feast].
(Va.3.20) One learned in the four <s>Vedas</s>, one skilled in dialectics, one who knows the <s>Vedāṅgas</s>, a teacher of <s>dharma</s>,
(Va.3.20) Three persons established in [their respective] <s>āśramas</s> — these are the foremost. An assembly [should consist of] not fewer than ten of them.

body.text: Va.3.21 upanīya(upa-nī-) kṛtsnam^vedam adhyāpayet(adhi-i-) sa ācāryas^(c)//
body.translated_text: (Va.3.21) One who, having initiated [the student], teaches the entire <s>Veda</s> — he is the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher).
(Va.3.22) But one who [teaches only] a portion — he is the <s>upādhyāya</s> (sub-teacher).
(Va.3.23) And [likewise one who teaches] the <s>Vedāṅgas</s>.

body.text: Va.3.24 ātma.trāṇe varṇa.saṃvarge brāhmaṇa.vaiśyau śastram ādadīyātām(ā-dā-) //
body.translated_text: (Va.3.24) For self-protection, in a time of caste-mixing (<s>varṇasaṃvarga</s>), a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and a <s>Vaiśya</s> may take up arms.

body.text: Va.3.25 kṣatriyasya tu tat^nityam eva rakṣaṇa.adhikārāt //
body.translated_text: (Va.3.25) But for the <s>Kṣatriya</s>, that [bearing of arms] is always [prescribed], because of his authority over protection.

body.text: Va.3.26 prakṣālya(pra-kṣal-) pādau pāṇī ca^ā maṇi.bandhāt prāk^vā^udak^vā^āsīnas^aṅguṣṭha.mūlasya^uttara.rekhā brāhmam^tīrtham^tena tris^ācāmet(ā-cam-)^a.śabda.vat //
body.translated_text: (Va.3.26) Having washed both feet and both hands up to the wrist, sitting facing east or north, at the line at the base of the thumb — that is the <s>Brāhma tīrtha</s> (sacred spot). With that, one should sip water (<s>ācamana</s>) three times, without making a sound.
(Va.3.27) One should wipe [the lips] twice.
(Va.3.28) One should touch the [bodily] openings with water.
(Va.3.29) One should direct water onto the head and onto the left hand.
(Va.3.30) While walking, during meals, lying down, or bowing — one should not perform <s>ācamana</s>.
(Va.3.31) A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [sips] with water that reaches the heart, without bubbles, without foam.
(Va.3.32) A <s>Kṣatriya</s>, with [water] that reaches the throat.
(Va.3.33) A <s>Vaiśya</s>, with water [merely] tasted.
(Va.3.34) A woman and a <s>Śūdra</s>, with water [merely] touched.

body.text: Va.3.35 pradarāt^api yās^gos taparṇa.samarthās^syus(as-)^//{BṣPṣ taparṇa}{F tarpaṇa}
body.translated_text: (Va.3.35) Even from a waterfall, [waters] that are sufficient for the satisfaction of a cow [are acceptable].
(Va.3.36) Not [waters] that are corrupted in color, smell, or taste, nor those that are of impure origin.
(Va.3.37) The chief [water-]drops do not render [food] leftover (<s>ucchiṣṭa</s>), [provided they are] not touched by a limb.

body.text: Va.3.38 suptvā(svap-) bhuktvā(bhuj-) kṣutvā(kṣu-) pītvā(pā-) ruditvā(rud-) snātvā(snā-) ca^antas^punar^ācāmet(ā-cam-)^vāsas^ca paridhāya(pari-dhā-) //
body.translated_text: (Va.3.38) After sleeping, eating, sneezing, drinking, weeping, and bathing, one should again perform <s>ācamana</s> inwardly, and also after putting on a garment.
(Va.3.39) Having touched the lips where they are hairless.
(Va.3.40) Not [food particles] adhering to the beard.
(Va.3.41) Like [food lodged between] the teeth — what is stuck in the teeth or what is inside the mouth, if one swallows it — even then one is pure. Thus.
(Va.3.42) When one causes others to perform <s>ācamana</s>, the drops that fall on the feet —

body.text: Va.3.42 tābhis^na^ucchiṣṭatām^yānti(yā-) bhūmyās tās tu samās^smṛtās^(c)//
body.translated_text: (Va.3.42) By those [drops] one does not become impure (<s>ucchiṣṭa</s>); they are considered equal to [water on] the ground.
(Va.3.43) If, while moving about during meals, one touches leftover [food] (<s>ucchiṣṭa</s>),

body.text: Va.3.43 bhūmau nidhāya(ni-dhā-) tat^dravyām ācamya(ā-cam-) pracaret(pra-car-) punas^(c)//
body.translated_text: (Va.3.43) Having placed that object on the ground and having performed <s>ācamana</s>, one may proceed again.
(Va.3.44) Whatever is subject to doubt, one should touch with water.
(Va.3.45) Wild animals killed by dogs, fruit dropped by birds,
(Va.3.45) What has been walked over by children, and what has been handled by women,

body.text: Va.3.46 prasāritam^ca yat paṇyam^ye doṣās^strī.mukheṣu ca (c)//
body.translated_text: (Va.3.46) Merchandise that has been displayed, and defects [found] on women's faces,
(Va.3.47) [Food] is not rendered impure by mosquitoes and flies that have alighted upon it.
(Va.3.47) And waters that rest upon the ground, and those that satisfy cows —

body.text: Va.3.47 parisaṃkhyāya(pari-sam-khyā-) tān sarvān^śucīn āha(ah-) prajāpatis.(c) iti //
body.translated_text: (Va.3.47) Having considered all these, <s>Prajāpati</s> declared them pure. Thus [ends the citation].
(Va.3.48) Purification [consists in] the removal of stain and smell. [The purification] of what is smeared with impure [substances is effected] with water and earth.
(Va.3.49) For [objects made of] metal, clay, wood, and woven material — [purification is by] ashes, rubbing, burning, planing, and washing [respectively].
(Va.3.50) For [objects of] stone and gems, as for metal.
(Va.3.51) For conch and mother-of-pearl, as for gems.
(Va.3.52) For bone, as for wood.
(Va.3.53) For rope, split bamboo, and leather, purification is as for cloth.
(Va.3.54) For [objects] made of fruit [shells], with cow-tail [brushes].
(Va.3.55) For flaxen and woolen [items], with a paste of white mustard.

body.text: Va.3.56 bhūmes tu saṃmārjana.upalena.ullekhana.prokṣaṇa.upakarṇais^yathā.sthānam^doṣa.viśeṣāt prāyatyam upaiti(upa-i-) //{BṣPṣ upalena}{E upalepana}
body.translated_text: (Va.3.56) For the ground — sweeping, plastering, scraping, sprinkling, and smearing — each according to its [proper] place and according to the particular impurity, it attains purity.
(Va.3.57) And moreover they cite:
(Va.3.57) By digging, by burning, by rubbing, and by the treading of cows —
(Va.3.57) By these four the ground is purified, and fifthly by plastering.

body.text: Va.3.58 rajasā śudhyate(śudh-) nārī nadī vegena śudhyate(śudh-) (c)/
body.translated_text: (Va.3.58) A woman is purified by her menstrual period; a river is purified by its current;
(Va.3.58) Bronze is purified by ashes; an earthen [vessel] by re-firing.
(Va.3.59) [A vessel] touched by liquor, urine, excrement, phlegm, pus, tears, or blood —
(Va.3.59) An earthen [vessel] so touched cannot be purified even by re-firing.
(Va.3.60) The limbs are purified by water; the mind is purified by truth;
(Va.3.60) The embodied self is purified by learning and austerity; the intellect is purified by knowledge. Thus [ends the citation].
(Va.3.61) Gold is purified by water alone.
(Va.3.62) Likewise silver.
(Va.3.63) Copper is purified by acid.
(Va.3.64) At the base of the little finger is the <s>Daiva tīrtha</s> (sacred spot for the gods).
(Va.3.65) At the tips of the fingers is [the <s>tīrtha</s>] of the <s>Ṛṣis</s> (sages).
(Va.3.66) At the fingertips is the <s>Mānuṣa</s> (human) [<s>tīrtha</s>].
(Va.3.67) In the center of the palm is the <s>Āgneya</s> (fire) [<s>tīrtha</s>].
(Va.3.68) Between the forefinger and the thumb is the <s>Pitrya</s> (ancestral) [<s>tīrtha</s>].
(Va.3.69) 'It is pleasing' — with [this word] one should honor the morning and evening meals.
(Va.3.70) 'It is well-flavored' — [thus one says] at ancestral [rites].
(Va.3.71) 'It is abundant' — [thus one says] at ceremonies of prosperity. Thus.
(Va.4.1) The four-caste system (<s>cāturvarṇya</s>) is distinguished by [both] origin (<s>prakṛti</s>) and particular sacraments (<s>saṃskāra</s>).
(Va.4.2) 'The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> was his mouth, the <s>Rājanya</s> (Kṣatriya) was made from his arms,

body.text: Va.4.2 urū tat^asya yat^vaiśyas^padbhyām^śūdro ajāyata(jan-) (c)//{BṣPṣ urū}{F ūrū}{śūdro < śūdras}
body.translated_text: (Va.4.2) His thighs were the <s>Vaiśya</s>; from his feet the <s>Śūdra</s> was born.'
(Va.4.2) Thus is also a Vedic text (<s>nigama</s>).

body.text: Va.4.3 gāyatryā brāhmaṇam asṛjata(sṛj-) triṣṭubhā rājanyam^jagatyā vaiśyam^na kena.cit^chandasā śūdram iti^a.saṃskāryas^vijñāyate(vi-jñā-) //
body.translated_text: (Va.4.3) 'He created the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> with the <s>Gāyatrī</s> [meter], the <s>Rājanya</s> with the <s>Triṣṭubh</s>, the <s>Vaiśya</s> with the <s>Jagatī</s>; the <s>Śūdra</s> [was not created] with any meter' — thus [the <s>Śūdra</s>] is known to be without [Vedic] sacrament.
(Va.4.4) For all [castes]: truthfulness, absence of anger, generosity, non-violence, and procreation.
(Va.4.5) 'One may kill an animal only in the worship of ancestors, gods, and guests' — thus is the rule of <s>Manu</s>.

body.text: Va.4.6 madhuparke ca yajñe ca pitṛ.daivata.karmaṇi (c)/
body.translated_text: (4.6) At the honey-mixture (<s>madhu-parka</s>), at a sacrifice, and in rites for the ancestors and the gods—
(4.6) only on these occasions should one kill an animal, and not otherwise—so declared <s>Manu</s>.
(4.7) Meat is never produced without harm to living beings;

body.text: Va.4.7 na ca prāṇi.vadhas^svargyas tasmāt^yāge vadhas^avadhas^(c)//
body.translated_text: (4.7) and the killing of living beings does not lead to heaven. Therefore, killing in a sacrifice is not [truly] killing.

body.text: Va.4.8 atha^api brāhmaṇāya vā rājanyāya vā^abhyāgatāya mahā.ukṣāṇam^vā mahā.ajam^vā pacet(pac-)^evam asmai^ātithyam^kurvanti(kṛ-)^iti //
body.translated_text: (4.8) Moreover, for a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> or a <s>Kṣatriya</s> who arrives as a guest, one should cook a large bull or a large goat—thus they perform hospitality for him.
(4.9) Water-offerings and purification [apply for a deceased child] from the age of two years onward.
(4.10) Until the cutting of the teeth, according to some.
(4.11) Having committed the body to the fire, without looking back, they should enter the waters.

body.text: Va.4.12 savya.itarābhyām^pāṇibhyam udaka.kriyām^kurvīran(kṛ-)^a.yugmāsu dakṣiṇā.mukhās^//{BṣPṣ pāṇibhyam}{F pāṇibhyām}
body.translated_text: (4.12) With both hands—right and left—they should perform the water-offering on odd [days], facing south.
(4.13) For the direction of the ancestors (<s>pitṛs</s>) is indeed the southern direction.

body.text: Va.4.14 gṛhān vrajitvā(vraj-) prastare tri.aham an.aśnantas(aś-)^āsīran(ās-) //
body.translated_text: (4.14) Having gone home, they should sit on [a bed of] grass for three days without eating.
(4.15) If unable, they may subsist on purchased or naturally produced [food].
(4.16) A period of ten days of death-impurity (<s>śāva āśauca</s>) is prescribed for <s>sapiṇḍa</s> relatives.
(4.17) <s>Sapiṇḍa</s> relationship is understood to extend through seven generations of men (<s>sa-āpta-puruṣa</s>).
(4.18) For married women, [the <s>sapiṇḍa</s> relationship] is understood to extend through three generations.
(4.19) For married women, the [relatives of the] other [family] should perform [the rites]; and those [married women observe impurity] for them [the husband's family].
(4.20) At a birth, the same rule applies for those who desire precise purification.
(4.21) Or [the birth-impurity applies to] the mother and father [alone].
(4.22) Because the mother is the cause [of the birth], according to some.
(4.23) Moreover, they cite [the following]:
(4.23) There is no impurity for a man at childbirth, if he does not come into contact [with the mother];

body.text: Va.4.23 rajas tatra^aśuci jñeyam^tat^ca puṃṣi na vidyate(vid-).(c) iti //
body.translated_text: (4.23) the menstrual discharge there is to be known as impure, and that does not exist in a man.
(4.24) If within that [period of impurity] another [death or birth] should occur, they become pure by the remainder [of the original period].
(4.25) If the remainder is [only] two nights, [they become pure] in two [nights].
(4.26) If [the news comes] at dawn, in three [nights].
(4.27) A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [becomes pure] after ten nights.
(4.28) A <s>Kṣatriya</s> after fifteen nights.
(4.29) A <s>Vaiśya</s> after twenty nights.
(4.30) A <s>Śūdra</s> becomes pure after a month.
(4.31) Moreover, they cite [the following]:

body.text: Va.4.31 aśauce yas tu śūdrasya sūtake vā^api bhuktavān(bhuj-) (c)/
body.translated_text: (4.31) One who eats during the impurity of a <s>Śūdra</s>, or during [his] birth-impurity,
(4.31) goes to a terrible hell and is born in animal wombs.
(4.32) A twice-born (<s>dvija</s>) who, by compulsion, has eaten during [the first] ten days after another's death—

body.text: Va.4.32 kṛmis^bhūtvā(bhū-) sa deha.ante tām^viṣṭhām^samupāśnute(sam-up-aś-).(c) iti //
body.translated_text: (4.32) having become a worm at the end of [that] body, he consumes that very excrement.

body.text: Va.4.33 dvādaśa māsān dvādaśa^ardhamāsān vā^an.aśnan(aś-) saṃhitā.adhyayanam adhīyānas(adhi-i-)^pūtas^bhavati(bhū-)^iti vijñāyate(vi-jñā-) //
body.translated_text: (4.33) It is known that one who fasts for twelve months or twelve half-months, studying the <s>Saṃhitā</s>, becomes purified.

body.text: Va.4.34 ūna.dvi.varṣe prete(pra-i-) garbha.patane vā sapiṇḍānām^tri.rātram āśaucam //
body.translated_text: (4.34) When a [child] under two years of age dies, or in the case of a miscarriage, the death-impurity for the <s>sapiṇḍa</s> relatives lasts three nights.
(4.35) Immediate purification, according to <s>Gautama</s>.
(4.36) When someone dies while residing in another country, and [the relatives] hear of it after ten days, the impurity lasts one night.

body.text: Va.4.37 āhitāgnis^cet pravasan(pra-vas-) mriyeta(mṛ-) punar^saṃskāram^kṛtvā(kṛ-) śavavat.śaucam iti gautamas^//
body.translated_text: (4.37) If one who has established the sacred fires dies while on a journey, after performing the funeral rites again, the impurity is as for a [normal] corpse—according to <s>Gautama</s>.

(4.38) After touching a sacrificial post (<s>yūpa</s>), a funerary mound (<s>citi</s>), a cremation ground, a menstruating woman, or a woman who has just given birth—or any impure person—one should immerse [in water] including the head, [reciting] '<s>āpas</s>.'
(5.1) A woman is not independent; she is subordinate to man.
(5.2) A woman without fire-rites or without menses is known as [one who has attained] immortality (<s>amṛta</s>).
(5.3) Moreover, they cite [the following]:

body.text: Va.5.3 pitā rakṣati(rakṣ-) kaumāre bhartā rakṣati(rakṣ-) yauvane (c)/
body.translated_text: (5.3) The father protects her in childhood, the husband protects her in youth,

body.text: Va.5.3 putras^ca sthavire bhāve na strī svātantryam arhati(arh-).(c) iti //
body.translated_text: (5.3) and the sons in old age—a woman does not deserve independence.
(5.4) Her sorcery (<s>abhicāra</s>) against her husband—the prescribed expiation has been stated in the secret [texts].
(5.5) For month by month, their menstruation removes their sins.
(5.6) A menstruating woman is impure for three nights.

body.text:
Va.5.7 sā na^añjyāt(añj-)^na^abhyañjyāt(abhi-añj-)^na^apsu snāyāt(snā-)^adhas^śayīta(śī-) na divā svapyāt(svap-)^na^agnim^spṛśet(spṛś-)^na rañjum^sṛjet(sṛj-)^na dantān dhāvayet(dhāv-)^na māṃsam aśnīyāt(aś-)^na grahān nirīkṣeta(nir-īkṣ-) na haset(has-)^na kiṃcetad ācaret(ā-car-)^na dhāvetad akharveṇa pātreṇa pibet(pā-)^añjalinā vā pibet(pā-)^lohita.ayasena
vā //{BṣPṣ kiṃcetad}{F kiṃcid}{BṣPṣ dhāvetad}{F dhāved(dhāv-)}
body.translated_text: (5.7) She should not apply ointment, nor massage herself, nor bathe in [standing] water; she should sleep on the ground, not sleep during the day, not touch fire, not spin thread, not clean her teeth, not eat meat, not look at the planets, not laugh, not engage in any [household] activity, not run; she should drink from an unchipped vessel or drink from her cupped hands, or from an iron [vessel].

body.text:
Va.5.8 vijñāyate(vi-jñā-) hi / indras triśīrṣāṇam^tvāṣṭram^hatvā(han-) pāpma.gṛhītas^mahattama.adharma.saṃbaddhas^aham iti^evam ātmānam amanyata(man-) / tam^sarvāṇi bhūtāni^abhyakrośan(abhi-kruś-) bhrūṇahan bhrūṇahan^iti / sa striyas^upādhāvat^asyai me bhrūṇahatyāyai tṛtīyam^bhāgam^pratigṛhṇīta(prati-gṛh-)^iti / tā abravan(brū-) kim^no bhūyāt(bhū-)^iti
/ sas^abravīt(brū-)^varam^vṛṇīdhvam(vṛ-) iti / tās^abruvan(brū-)^ṛtau prajām^vindāmahe(vid-)^iti kāmam ā vijanitos^saṃbhavāma(sam-bhū-)^iti / tathā^iti tās^pratijagṛhus^sā^eṣā bhrūṇahatyā māsi-māsi^āvis^bhavati(bhū-) tasmāt^rajasvalāyā annam^na^aśnīyāt(aś-)^bhrūṇahatyāyā eva^eṣā rūpam^pratimucya(prati-muc-)^āste //
body.translated_text: (5.8) For it is known: <s>Indra</s>, having slain <s>Triśīrṣa</s> [Tvaṣṭar's son], was seized by sin and thought to himself: 'I am connected with the greatest transgression, as a slayer of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> (<s>bhrūṇahan</s>).' All beings reviled him, [saying:] '<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>-slayer! <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>-slayer!' He approached women [and said:] 'Accept one-third of this sin of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>-slaying for me.' They said: 'What shall be ours [in return]?' He said: 'Choose a boon.' They said: 'May we obtain offspring during the fertile season; may we unite [with men] as we desire until childbirth.' 'So be it,' they accepted. That very sin of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>-slaying becomes manifest month by month. Therefore, one should not eat the food of a menstruating woman—for she sits having assumed the form of the sin of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>-slaying.

body.text: Va.5.9 tat^āhur(ah-)^/ añjana.abhyañjanam eva^asyās^na pratigrāhyam^tat^hi striyās^annam iti / tasmāt tasyai ca tatra ca bībhatsante(bhī-) mā^iyam upāgāt(upa-ā-gā-)^iti //
body.translated_text: (5.9) Therefore they say: Even ointment and massage from her should not be accepted, for that is a woman's food. Therefore, [people] feel disgust toward her in that [condition], [thinking:] 'Let her not approach!'

body.text: Va.5.10 udakyās tu^āsate(ās-) yeṣām^ye ca ke.cit^anagnayas^(c)/
body.translated_text: (5.10) Those among whom menstruating women sit, and whosoever are without sacred fires,

body.text: Va.5.10 kulam^ca^aśrotriyām yeṣām^sarve te śūdra.dharmiṇas.(c) iti //
body.translated_text: (5.10) and those whose family has no Vedic learning—all of them follow the dharma of <s>Śūdras</s>.
(5.10) All of them follow the dharma of <s>Śūdras</s>.
(6.1) Conduct (<s>ācāra</s>) is the supreme dharma—this is the settled view for all;

body.text: Va.6.1 hīna.ācāra.parīta.ātmā pretya(pra-i-) ca^iha ca naśyati(naś-) (c)//
body.translated_text: (6.1) one whose self is surrounded by degraded conduct perishes both in the next world and in this.

body.text: Va.6.2 na^enam^tapāṃsi na brahma na^agnihotram^na dakṣiṇās^(c)/
body.translated_text: (6.2) Neither austerities, nor Vedic study, nor the fire sacrifice (<s>agnihotra</s>), nor sacrificial gifts,
(6.2) can in any way save one of degraded conduct who has fallen from here.
(6.3) The <s>Vedas</s> do not purify one who lacks [proper] conduct, even if studied together with the six <s>Vedāṅgas</s>;
(6.3) the [Vedic] meters abandon him at the time of death, like fledgling birds leaving a nest.

body.text: Va.6.4 ācāra.hīnasya tu brāhmaṇasya vedās^ṣaṭ.aṅgās tu^akhilās^sa.yajñās^(c)/
body.translated_text: (6.4) For a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who lacks [proper] conduct, the entire <s>Vedas</s> with six <s>Vedāṅgas</s> together with sacrifices—
(6.4) what pleasure can they produce? Like beautiful wives for a blind man.

body.text: Va.6.5 na^enam^chandāṃsi vṛjināt tārayanti(tṛ-) māyāvinam^māyayā vartamānam(vṛt-) (c)/
body.translated_text: (6.5) The [Vedic] meters do not save from sin one who is deceitful, living by deceit;

body.text: Va.6.5 dve^api^akṣare samyak^adhīyamāne(adhi-i-) punāti(pū-) tat^brahma yathā iṣe^abdās^(c)//
body.translated_text: (6.5) even two syllables properly studied purify—that <s>Brahman</s> [purifies], as [the sound] '<s>yathā iṣe</s>' [illustrates the power of correct utterance].
(6.6) A man of bad conduct becomes despised in the world,
(6.6) and is constantly subject to suffering, afflicted with disease, and of short life indeed.

body.text: Va.6.7 ācārāt phalate(phal-) dharmas^ācārāt phalate(phal-) dhanam (c)/
body.translated_text: (6.7) From [good] conduct, dharma bears fruit; from conduct, wealth bears fruit;
(6.7) from conduct one obtains prosperity; [good] conduct destroys ill-fortune.
(6.8) A man devoid of all [auspicious] marks, but who possesses good conduct,
(6.8) who is faithful and free from envy—he lives a hundred years.
(6.9) Food-intake, excretion, recreation, and exercise should be well-regulated and performed by one who knows the dharma;

body.text: Va.6.9 vāc.buddhi.kāryāṇi tapas tathā^eva dhana.āyuṣī guptatame tu kārye (c)//
body.translated_text: (6.9) activities of speech, intellect, and body, as well as austerity—but wealth and lifespan should be kept most secret.
(6.10) Both urine and excrement one should discharge during the day facing north;

body.text: Va.6.10 rātrau tu dakṣiṇā kuryāt(kṛ-)^evam^hi^āyus^na riṣyati(riṣ-) (c)//
body.translated_text: (6.10) at night, one should [discharge them] facing south—thus one's lifespan is not harmed.

body.text: Va.6.11 prati^agnim^prati sūryam^ca prati gām^prati brāhmaṇam (c)/
body.translated_text: (6.11) Facing the fire, facing the sun, facing a cow, facing a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>,
(6.11) facing the moon, water, or the twilight junction (<s>sandhyā</s>)—one who urinates [in these directions] destroys his wisdom.

body.text: Va.6.12 na nadyām^mehanam^kuryāt(kṛ-)^na pathi na ca bhasmani (c)/
body.translated_text: (6.12) One should not urinate in a river, nor on a path, nor on ashes,

body.text: Va.6.12 na go.maye na kṛṣṭe na^upte na śādvala.upajīvya.chāyāsu //
body.translated_text: (6.12) nor on cow-dung, nor on ploughed or sown [land], nor in the shade of grass or [trees] that provide livelihood.

body.text: Va.6.13 chāyāyām andhakāre vā rātrau^ahani vā dvijas^(c)/
body.translated_text: (6.13) In shade, in darkness, at night or by day, a twice-born (<s>dvija</s>)
(6.13) may [urinate] facing whichever direction is comfortable, and in times of danger to life.
(6.14) Ritual acts should be performed with drawn [i.e., elevated] water.
(6.15) Bathing, however, [may be done] even with undrawn water.
(6.16) A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should fetch earth from a river-bank—that which contains sand.
(6.17) [Earth from] underwater, from a temple, from an anthill, from a mouse-hole,
(6.17) and [earth] left over from a previous purification—these five [kinds of] earth should not be taken.
(6.18) One [application of earth] on the male organ, three on the hand, two [applications of earth] on both [hands], is prescribed;
(6.18) five on the posterior, ten on one [hand], and seven [applications of earth] on both [hands].
(6.19) This is the purification for householders; it is doubled for celibate students (<s>brahmacārins</s>);
(6.19) tripled for forest-dwellers (<s>vānaprasthas</s>); and quadrupled for renunciants (<s>yatis</s>).
(6.20) Eight morsels are the meal of an ascetic (<s>muni</s>); sixteen for a forest-dweller;
(6.20) thirty-two for a householder; and unlimited for a celibate student.

body.text: Va.6.21 āhitāgnis^anaḍvān^ca brahmacārī ca te trayas^(c)/
body.translated_text: (6.21) One who has established the fires (<s>āhitāgni</s>), a draft-ox, and a celibate student—these three
(6.21) succeed precisely by eating; there is no success for them in not eating.
(6.22) [This applies] in vows, observances, and the duties of sacrifice and study.
(6.23) Yoga, austerity, self-control, giving, truthfulness, purity, learning, compassion,
(6.23) knowledge, wisdom, and faith in [the authority of scripture]—this is the mark of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.
(6.24) Long-lasting enmity, envy, untruthfulness, and fault-finding with <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>,
(6.24) tale-bearing and cruelty—one should recognize these as the marks of a <s>Śūdra</s>.
(6.25) Those who are peaceful, disciplined, whose ears are filled with scripture, who have conquered the senses, who have turned away from the killing of living beings,

body.text: Va.6.25 pratigrahe saṅkucita.agra.hastās te brāhmaṇās tārayitum(tṛ-)^samarthās^(c)//
body.translated_text: (6.25) whose hands are reluctant to accept gifts—those <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> are able to save [others].
(6.26) Some receptacles [for gifts] are filled with the <s>Vedas</s>; some receptacles are filled with austerity;

body.text: Va.6.26 pātrāṇām api tat pātram^śūdra.annam^yasya na^udare (c)//
body.translated_text: (6.26) but that is [the best] receptacle among receptacles—[the one] in whose stomach there is no <s>Śūdra</s>-food.
(6.27) If any twice-born (<s>dvija</s>) dies with <s>Śūdra</s>-food in his stomach,

body.text: Va.6.27 sa bhavet(bhū-)^śūkaras^grāmyas tasya vā jāyate(jan-) kule (c)//
body.translated_text: (6.27) he will become a village pig, or will be born in that [<s>Śūdra</s>'s] family.
(6.28) One whose limbs are nourished by the essence of <s>Śūdra</s>-food, even though he constantly studies,

body.text: Va.6.28 juhvan(hu-) vā^api japan(jap-) vā^api gatim ūrdhvām^na vindati(vid-) (c)//
body.translated_text: (6.28) or offers oblations, or mutters prayers—he does not attain the upward path.
But he who, having eaten the food of a <s>Śūdra</s>, engages in sexual intercourse,

body.text: Va.6.29 yasya^annam^tasya te putrās^na ca svarga.āruhas^bhavet(bhū-) (c)//
body.translated_text: His children belong to the one whose food [he ate]; nor will he ascend to heaven.
One devoted to <s>svādhyāya</s> (self-study), endowed with sacred formulas, tranquil, maintaining the sacred fires (<s>vaitāna</s>), fearing sin, learned in many subjects,
Patient with women, righteous, a protector of cows, worn out by observances—such a one they call a worthy recipient.
Just as milk, curds, ghee, and honey placed in a raw vessel

body.text: Va.6.31 vinaśyet(vi-naś-) pātra.daurbalyāt^na ca pātram^rasās^ca te (c)//
body.translated_text: Would be ruined by the weakness of the vessel—and neither the vessel nor those liquids [survive],
So too, cows, gold, cloth, horses, land, and sesame seeds—
An unlearned man accepting them becomes ashes, like a piece of wood.
One should not play with one's limbs or nails.
Nor [scratch] with nails at the beginning of a meal.
Nor should one drink water with cupped hands (<s>añjali</s>).

body.text: Va.6.36 na pādena pāṇinā vā jalam abhihanyāt(abhi-han-) //
body.translated_text: Nor should one strike water with the foot or with the hand.
Nor [should one strike] water with water.
Nor should one knock down a fruit with bricks.
Nor [should one strike] a fruit with a fruit.
One should not be a cheat or a juggler.
One should not learn the language of <s>Mlecchas</s> (barbarians).
Moreover, they cite [the following]:
One should not be restless with hands and feet, nor restless with the eyes,

body.text: Va.6.42 na ca vāc.aṅga.capalas^iti śiṣṭasya gocaras^(c)//
body.translated_text: Nor restless in speech and body—such is the conduct of a cultured person (<s>śiṣṭa</s>).
Those to whom the <s>Veda</s> together with its supplements has come down in unbroken succession,
They are to be known as the cultured <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, having <s>śruti</s> (scripture), direct perception, and reasoning as their authorities.
He whom no one knows as either good or bad, as either unlearned or learned,

body.text: Va.6.44 na su.vṛttam^na dur.vṛttam^veda kas.cit sa brāhmaṇas^(c)//
body.translated_text: As either well-conducted or ill-conducted—he is [a true] <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.
He is [a true] <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>—thus.
There are four <s>āśramas</s> (stages of life).
The <s>Brahmacārin</s> (student), the <s>Gṛhastha</s> (householder), the <s>Vānaprastha</s> (forest-dweller), and the <s>Parivrājaka</s> (wandering ascetic).

body.text: Va.7.3 teṣām^vedam adhītya(adhi-i-) vedau vedān vā^a.viśīrṇa.brahmacaryas^yam icchet(iṣ-) tam āvaset(ā-vas-) //
body.translated_text: Having studied one <s>Veda</s>, two <s>Vedas</s>, or [all] the <s>Vedas</s>, with his celibacy unbroken, he may enter whichever [<s>āśrama</s>] he wishes.
The <s>Brahmacārin</s> should serve the teacher until the dissolution of the body.
And if the teacher dies, he should serve the [sacred] fire.
For it is known [from scripture]: 'The fire is your teacher.'
He should be restrained in speech.
He should eat at the fourth, sixth, or eighth meal-time.
He should go on begging rounds (<s>bhaikṣa</s>).
He should be dependent on the teacher.
He should wear matted hair, or a topknot with matted hair.
He should follow the teacher when he walks; if [the teacher is] seated, he should stand; if [the teacher is] lying down, he should sit nearby and attend upon him.
He should study only when called upon.
Having offered everything obtained [to the teacher], he should eat with the teacher's permission.
He should abstain from a bed, tooth-cleaning sticks, washing [the body with cosmetics], ointment for the eyes, oil-anointing, sandals, and an umbrella.
He should stand during the day and sit during the night.
Three times a day he should approach the waters [for ritual bathing], [reciting] 'waters, waters.'

The householder (<s>Gṛhastha</s>), having controlled anger and elation, permitted by the teacher, having bathed [i.e., completed studentship], should take a wife who is not of the same <s>gotra</s> (lineage), who has not been previously touched [by another man], who is younger in age, and who is of equal [social standing].
[She should be] removed by five [degrees] from the mother's relatives and by seven from the father's relatives.
He should kindle the wedding fire.
He should not turn away a guest who has arrived in the evening.
No [guest] should dwell in his house without eating.

body.text: Va.8.6 yasya na^aśnāti(aś-) vāsa.arthī brāhmaṇas^gṛham āgatas^(c)/
body.translated_text: If a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who has come to his house seeking lodging does not eat,

body.text: Va.8.6 sukṛtam^tasya yat kim.cit sarvam ādāya(ā-dā-) gacchati(gam-) (c)//
body.translated_text: He takes away all of whatever merit that [householder] has, and departs.
A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who stays for one night is considered a guest;
Since he stays impermanently, he is called '<s>atithi</s>' (guest) [lit. 'without a fixed date'].
A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> from the same village is not a guest, nor is a travelling companion;

body.text: Va.8.8 kāle prāpte akāle vā na^asya^an.aśnan(aś-) gṛhe vaset(vas-) (c)//
body.translated_text: Whether [the guest] arrives at the proper or improper time, he should not dwell in his house without eating.
He should be of faithful disposition, free from covetousness; he should be fully capable of establishing the sacred fires (<s>agnyādhāna</s>) and should not be one who has not established them.
He should be fully capable of performing the <s>Soma</s> sacrifice, and should not be one who has not sacrificed with <s>Soma</s>.
He should be devoted to self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>), sacrifice (<s>yajña</s>), and procreation.
A guest who has arrived at the house should be honored with rising from one's seat, offering a seat, kind words, truthful speech, and freedom from envy.
And all beings [should be served] with food, to the best of one's ability.

body.text: Va.8.14 gṛhasthas^eva yajate(yaj-) gṛhasthas tapyate(tap-) tapas^(c)/
body.translated_text: The householder alone sacrifices, the householder alone performs austerity;
Among the four <s>āśramas</s>, the householder is pre-eminent.

body.text: Va.8.15 yathā nadī.nadās^sarve samudre yānti(yā-) saṃsthitim (c)/
body.translated_text: Just as all rivers and streams find their rest in the ocean,

body.text: Va.8.15 evam āśramiṇas^sarve gṛhasthe yānti(yā-) saṃsthitim (c)//
body.translated_text: So all those in the [other] stages of life find their rest in the householder.

body.text: Va.8.16 yathā mātaram āśritya(ā-śri-) sarve jīvanti(jīv-) jantavas^(c)/
body.translated_text: Just as all living creatures survive by depending upon their mother,

body.text: Va.8.16 evam^gṛhastham āśritya(ā-śri-) sarve jīvanti(jīv-) bhikṣukās^(c)//
body.translated_text: So all mendicants survive by depending upon the householder.
One who always carries water, always wears the sacred thread (<s>yajñopavīta</s>), is always devoted to self-study, and avoids the food of the fallen—

body.text: Va.8.17 ṛtau ca gacchan(gam-) vidhivat^ca juhvan(hu-) na brāhmaṇas^cyavate(cyu-) brahma.lokāt (c)//
body.translated_text: Who approaches [his wife] at the proper season and offers oblations according to rule—such a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> does not fall from the world of <s>Brahman</s>.
From the world of <s>Brahman</s>—thus.
The forest-dweller (<s>Vānaprastha</s>) should wear matted hair and dress in bark garments and animal skins.
He should not enter a village.
He should not stand on ploughed ground.
He should gather uncultivated roots and fruits.
He should be celibate (<s>ūrdhvaretās</s>).
He should have a disposition of forbearance.
He should honor a guest who has come to his hermitage with roots, fruits, and alms-food.
He should give indeed, but should not accept.
He should touch water three times [a day for ritual purification].
Having established the fire with the <s>Śrāmaṇaka</s> [rite], he should be one who maintains the sacred fire.
He should dwell at the root of a tree. After six months, [he should become] without fire and without a dwelling.

body.text: Va.9.12 dadyāt(dā-)^deva.pitṛ.manuṣyebhyas^sa gacchet(gam-) svargam ānantyam iti^ānantyam //
body.translated_text: He should give to gods, ancestors, and human beings; he goes to heaven, to infinity—to infinity.
The wandering ascetic (<s>Parivrājaka</s>), having given the gift of fearlessness to all beings, should set forth.
Moreover, they cite [the following]:
The sage who goes about having given fearlessness to all beings—
For him too, there is never any fear from any being.

body.text: Va.10.3 abhayam^sarva.bhūtebhyas^dattvā(dā-) yas tu nivarttate(ni-vṛt-) (c)/{BṣPṣ nivarttate}{F nivartate}
body.translated_text: But he who, having given fearlessness to all beings, then turns back [from his vow],

body.text: Va.10.3 hanti(han-) jātān ajātān^ca dravyāṇi pratigṛhya(prati-grah-) ca (c)//
body.translated_text: Kills both the born and the unborn, and [is guilty of] accepting gifts [improperly].

body.text: Va.10.4 sannyaset(sam-ni-as-) sarva.karmāṇi vedam ekam^na sannyaset(sam-ni-as-) (c)/
body.translated_text: One should renounce all [ritual] actions, but one should not renounce the <s>Veda</s>;
By renouncing the <s>Veda</s>, one becomes a <s>Śūdra</s>; therefore one should not renounce the <s>Veda</s>.
The single syllable [<s>Oṃ</s>] is the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>; <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath-control) is the supreme austerity;
Begging is superior to fasting; compassion (<s>dayā</s>) is distinguished above giving. Thus.
He should be shaven-headed, without possessiveness, without acquisitions.
He should beg for alms at seven houses without premeditation.
[He should beg] when the smoke has ceased and the pestle is laid down.
He should be clad in a single garment.
Or, with a deerskin, his body covered with grass trimmed [to the length used] for cows.
He should sleep on the bare ground.
He should dwell in an impermanent abode.

body.text: Va.10.13 grāma.ante deva.gṛhe śūnya.agāre vā vṛkṣa.mūle vā //
body.translated_text: [He should stay] at the outskirts of a village, in a temple, in an empty house, or at the root of a tree.
He should mentally study the knowledge [of the self].
He should be constantly in the forest.
He should not wander about in the sight of domestic animals.
For one who is constantly in the forest, who has conquered his senses, who has turned away from the pleasures of all the senses,
Whose mind is absorbed in the contemplation of the self (<s>adhyātma</s>)—for such an equanimous one, the non-return [to this world] is assured. Thus.
He should have indistinct marks and indistinct conduct.
Not mad, yet having the appearance of a madman.
Moreover, they cite [the following]:

body.text:
Va.10.20 na śabda.śāstrabhiratasya mokṣas^na ca^api loka.grahaṇe ratasya (c)/{BṣPṣ śāstrabhiratasya}{F śāstra.abhiratasya}
Va.10.20 na bhojana.ācchādana.tatparasya na ca^api ramya.āvasatha.priyasya (c)//
body.translated_text: There is no liberation for one delighting in the science of words, nor for one delighting in winning over the world, nor for one intent on food and clothing, nor for one fond of pleasant dwellings.
Nor through portents and omens, nor through the science of constellations and bodily marks,
Nor through teaching and disputation should one ever seek alms.

body.text: Va.10.22 alābhe na viṣādī syāt(as-)^lābhe na^eva ca harṣayet(hṛṣ-) (c)/
body.translated_text: When not obtaining [alms], one should not be despondent; and when obtaining, one should not be elated;
One should have only enough for sustaining life, free from attachment to material things.

body.text: Va.10.23 na kuṭyām^na^udake saṅgas^na caile na tri.puṣkare (c)/
body.translated_text: No attachment to a hut, to water, to a garment, to a triple [walking-stick];

body.text: Va.10.23 na^agāre na^āsane na^anne yasya vai mokṣa.vid tu sas.(c) iti //
body.translated_text: No [attachment] to a house, to a seat, to food—he who [is free from these] is indeed a knower of liberation. Thus.

body.text: Va.10.24 brāhmaṇa.kule yāvat^labheta(labh-) tat^bhuñjīta(bhuj-) sāyam^prātar madhu.māṃsa.varjam //
body.translated_text: In a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> household, whatever he obtains, that he should eat, morning and evening, avoiding honey and meat.
And he should not eat to satiety.
Or he may dwell in a village.
He should be without crookedness, without deceit, without shelter, without restlessness.
And he should not engage in sensory contact with anything.
He should be equanimous toward all beings, by refraining from both harm and favor.

The abandonment of slander, jealousy, conceit, egoism, faithlessness, dishonesty, self-praise, disparagement of others, deceit, greed, delusion, anger, and envy—this is the prescribed <s>dharma</s> for all the <s>āśramas</s>.

Wearing the sacred thread, carrying a water vessel (<s>kamaṇḍalu</s>) in hand, pure, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> avoiding the food of a <s>Śūdra</s> does not fall from the world of <s>Brahman</s>—from the world of <s>Brahman</s>. Thus.
Six persons are worthy of the <s>arghya</s> (ceremonial welcome).
The sacrificial priest (<s>ṛtvij</s>), the bridegroom, the king, the paternal uncle, the <s>snātaka</s> (graduate), and the maternal uncle.

body.text: Va.11.3 vaiśvadevasya siddhasya sāyam^prātar gṛhya.agnau juhuyāt(hu-) //
body.translated_text: He should offer [a portion] of the cooked <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> offering, morning and evening, into the domestic fire.
He should present the <s>bali</s> (food offering) to the household deities.
Having given the first portion to a learned <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> (<s>śrotriya</s>) or next to a <s>Brahmacārin</s>, he should give [the offering] to the ancestors.
Then he should feed the guest—the most distinguished first, in order of precedence.
Among his own household members: the maiden, the child, the aged, the young, and the newly delivered woman [should eat first].
Then the other household members.
He should scatter [food] on the ground for dogs, <s>Cāṇḍālas</s>, the fallen, and crows.
Va.11.10 One should give to a <s>Śūdra</s> leftover food or food that is not leftover.
Va.11.11 The husband and wife should eat the remainder.

Va.11.12 If, after all the offerings have been made and the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> (offering to all the gods) completed by using everything up, a guest should arrive by cooking again, one should especially have food prepared for him.

Va.11.13 For it is known [in the scriptures]: '<s>Vaiśvānara</s> (the universal fire) enters the house in the form of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> guest; therefore they bring water. Food [comes] from the rains—that is the peace that people know.'
Va.11.14 Having fed him, one should sit near him.
Va.11.15 One should accompany [the guest] up to the boundary, or [at least until receiving] his leave.
Va.11.16 In the dark fortnight, from the fourth [day] onward, one should give [offerings] to the ancestors (<s>pitṛs</s>).

body.text: Va.11.17 pūrvedyus^brāhmaṇān sannipātya(sam-ni-pat-) yatīn gṛhasthān sādhūn vā^a.pariṇata.vayasas^vikarma.sthān^śrotriyān a.śiṣyān an.antevāsinas^//
body.translated_text: Va.11.17 On the preceding day, having assembled <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>—ascetics or virtuous householders, who are not of advanced age, who do not engage in forbidden occupations, who are learned in the <s>Vedas</s>, who have no students, and who have no resident pupils—
Va.11.18 one should also feed students who possess [good] qualities.
Va.11.19 Excluding the naked, those in white [i.e., ascetics of certain sects], eunuchs, the blind, those with discolored teeth, lepers, and those with deformed nails.
Va.11.20 And they also cite [the following]:
Va.11.20 If one who knows the mantras is afflicted with physical defects that defile the row (<s>paṅktidūṣaṇa</s>),
Va.11.20 <s>Yama</s> has declared him to be not defiling; he is indeed a purifier of the row (<s>paṅktipāvana</s>).
Va.11.21 At a <s>śrāddha</s>, the remnants of food should not be removed until the end of the day.
Va.11.21 For streams of nectar (<s>sudhā</s>) drip down; those for whom water [offerings] have not been made drink them.
Va.11.22 One should not clean up the remnants as long as the sun has not set.
Va.11.22 Streams of milk then flow, imperishable, for the benefit of the wandering [spirits].

body.text: Va.11.23 prāk saṃskārāt pramītānām^sva.vaṃśyānām iti sthitis^(c)/
body.translated_text: Va.11.23 For those of one's own lineage who died before the sacraments [were performed], this is the established rule:
Va.11.23 <s>Manu</s> has declared their share to be the two [kinds of] leftover food and remnants.
Va.11.24 The remnants fallen on the ground, the scattered offerings, and the water used for smearing—
Va.11.24 one should offer food to the departed (<s>pretas</s>) who are without offspring and without longevity.
Va.11.25 Food offered to the ancestors released from both hands—
Va.11.25 in the interval, the <s>Asuras</s> of evil mind lie in wait for it.
Va.11.26 Therefore, one should handle food that has been brought with a hand that is not empty.
Va.11.26 Or, having touched the meal, one should stand [guard over] both [kinds of] remnants.

body.text: Va.11.27 dvau daive pitṛ.kṛtye trīn ekaikam ubhayatra vā (c)//
body.translated_text: Va.11.27 Two [<s>Brāhmaṇas</s>] for the rite to the gods, three for the rite to the ancestors, or one for each of the two—

body.text: Va.11.27 bhojayet(bhuj-) su.samṛddhas^api na prasajjeta(pra-sañj-) vistare (c)//
body.translated_text: Va.11.27 one should feed [them]; even if well-to-do, one should not indulge in elaboration.
Va.11.28 Proper rites, [appropriate] place and time, purity, and the excellence of the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>—
Va.11.28 elaboration destroys these five; therefore one should avoid it.
Va.11.29 Or one may feed a single <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who has mastered the <s>Vedas</s>,
Va.11.29 endowed with learning and good conduct, free from all [disqualifying] marks.
Va.11.30 If one feeds a single [<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>] at a <s>śrāddha</s>, how would the divine portion be [arranged]?

body.text: Va.11.30 annam^pātre samuddhṛtya(sam-ud-hṛ-) sarvasya prakṛtasya tu (c)//
body.translated_text: Va.11.30 Having taken out food in a vessel for the entire prescribed [offering],
Va.11.31 and having placed it at a shrine of a deity, one should then proceed with the <s>śrāddha</s>.
Va.11.31 Or one may offer that food into the fire, or give it to a <s>brahmacārin</s> (student).
Va.11.32 As long as the food is hot, and as long as [the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>] eat in silence,
Va.11.32 so long do the ancestors eat—as long as the qualities of the oblation have not been mentioned.
Va.11.33 The qualities of the oblation should not be spoken of as long as the ancestors are not satisfied.
Va.11.33 After the ancestors are satisfied, one may then speak of the excellent oblation.

body.text: Va.11.34 niyuktas tu yatis^śrāddhe daive vā māṃsam utsṛjet(ud-sṛj-) (c)/
body.translated_text: Va.11.34 But an ascetic (<s>yati</s>) who is invited to a <s>śrāddha</s> or a rite to the gods should renounce meat.
Va.11.34 As many hairs as the animal has, so many times does he go to hell.

body.text: Va.11.35 trīṇi śrāddhe pavitrāṇi dauhitras^ku.tapas tilās^(c)/
body.translated_text: Va.11.35 Three things are purifying in a <s>śrāddha</s>: the daughter's son, <s>kuśa</s> grass, and sesame seeds.

body.text: Va.11.35 trīṇi ca^atra praśaṃsānti(pra-śaṃs-) śaucam a.krodham a.tvarām (c)//
body.translated_text: Va.11.35 And three things are praised therein: purity, absence of anger, and absence of haste.
Va.11.36 When the sun grows faint in the eighth part of the day,
Va.11.36 that time should be known as [the time of] <s>kuśa</s> grass [offerings] to the ancestors; what is given [then] is imperishable.
Va.11.37 One who engages in sexual intercourse after having given and eaten at a <s>śrāddha</s>—
Va.11.37 his ancestors subsist on his semen for that month.

body.text: Va.11.38 yas tatas^jāyate(jan-) garbhas^dattvā(dā-) bhuktvā(bhuj-) ca paitṛkam (c)/
body.translated_text: Va.11.38 The offspring that is conceived after having given and eaten at an ancestral rite—

body.text: Va.11.38 na sa vidyām^samāpnoti(sam-āp-) kṣīṇa.āyus^ca^eva jāyate(jan-) (c)//
body.translated_text: Va.11.38 he does not attain learning and is born with a shortened lifespan.
Va.11.39 The father, the grandfather, and the great-grandfather—
Va.11.39 they await the birth of a son, like birds [awaiting] the <s>pippala</s> fruit.

body.text: Va.11.40 madhu.māṃsais^ca śākais^ca payasā pāyasena ca (c)/
body.translated_text: Va.11.40 [Thinking:] 'With honey, meat, vegetables, milk, and rice pudding,

body.text: Va.11.40 eṣa nas^dāsyati(dā-) śrāddham^varṣāsu ca maghāsu ca (c)//
body.translated_text: Va.11.40 this [son] will give us a <s>śrāddha</s> during the rainy season and during the <s>Maghā</s> [constellation].'
Va.11.41 A son who perpetuates the lineage, who is ready for ancestral rites,
Va.11.41 who is devoted to gods and <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>—the forefathers rejoice in him.

body.text: Va.11.42 nandanti(nand-) pitaras tasya su.kṛṣṭais^iva karṣakās^(c)/
body.translated_text: Va.11.42 The ancestors of that one who, standing at <s>Gayā</s>, gives food, delight in him—
Va.11.42 like farmers [delighting] in well-plowed [fields]. By that, they are provided with sons. Thus it is said.
Va.11.43 And on the <s>Śrāvaṇī</s> and <s>Āgrahāyaṇī</s> [full moon days] and on the <s>Anvaṣṭakā</s> [day], one should give [offerings] to the ancestors.
Va.11.44 Or, when the [proper] materials, place, and <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> are present, there is no restriction of time.
Va.11.45 A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> must necessarily establish the sacred fires.

Va.11.46 And he should perform sacrifices with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new and full moon rites), the <s>Āgrayaṇa</s> offering, the <s>Cāturmāsya</s> (seasonal rites), the animal sacrifice, and the <s>Soma</s> sacrifice.
Va.11.47 For this is obligatory and is praised as [discharging] a debt.

body.text: Va.11.48 vijñāyate(vi-jñā-) hi / tribhis^ṛṇais^ṛṇavān brāhmaṇas^jāyate(jan-)^iti / yajñena devebhyas^prajayā pitṛbhyas^brahmacaryeṇa ṛṣibhyas^iti^eṣa vā^anṛṇas^yajvā yas^putrī brahmacaryavān iti //
body.translated_text: Va.11.48 For it is known [in the scriptures]: 'A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is born burdened with three debts.' By sacrifice [he repays the debt] to the gods, by offspring to the ancestors, by <s>brahmacarya</s> (studentship) to the sages. 'He indeed is free from debt who is a sacrificer, who has a son, and who has observed <s>brahmacarya</s>.'

body.text: Va.11.49 garbha.aṣṭameṣu brāhmaṇam upanayīta(upa-nī-) //{BṣPṣ garbha.aṣṭameṣu}{F garbhāt. aṣṭameṣu}
body.translated_text: Va.11.49 One should initiate (<s>upanayana</s>) a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> in the eighth year from conception.
Va.11.50 A <s>Rājanya</s> (prince) in the eleventh year from conception.
Va.11.51 A <s>Vaiśya</s> in the twelfth year from conception.
Va.11.52 The staff of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should be of <s>palāśa</s> wood.
Va.11.53 Or that of a <s>Kṣatriya</s> should be of <s>nyagrodha</s> (banyan) wood.
Va.11.54 Or that of a <s>Vaiśya</s> should be of <s>udumbara</s> (fig) wood.
Va.11.55 [The staff] of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should reach the hair [i.e., the top of the head].
Va.11.56 That of a <s>Kṣatriya</s> should reach the forehead.
Va.11.57 That of a <s>Vaiśya</s> should reach the nose.
Va.11.58 The girdle of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should be of <s>muñja</s> grass.
Va.11.59 That of a <s>Kṣatriya</s> should be a bowstring.
Va.11.60 That of a <s>Vaiśya</s> should be of hemp or flax.
Va.11.61 The upper garment of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should be a black antelope skin.
Va.11.62 That of a <s>Kṣatriya</s> should be a <s>ruru</s> deer skin.
Va.11.63 That of a <s>Vaiśya</s> should be a cow-skin or goat-skin.
Va.11.64 The garment of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should be white and unworn.
Va.11.65 That of a <s>Kṣatriya</s> should be dyed with <s>mañjiṣṭha</s> (madder).
Va.11.66 That of a <s>Vaiśya</s> should be dyed with turmeric or of silk.
Va.11.67 Or for all [classes], a woven cloth that is undyed [may be used].
Va.11.68 A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should beg for alms with [the word] '<s>bhavat</s>' (sir) placed at the beginning.
Va.11.69 A <s>Rājanya</s> with '<s>bhavat</s>' placed in the middle.
Va.11.70 A <s>Vaiśya</s> with '<s>bhavat</s>' placed at the end.
Va.11.71 The time [for initiation] of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> does not lapse until [the age of] sixteen.
Va.11.72 For a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, until [the age of] twenty-two.
Va.11.73 For a <s>Vaiśya</s>, until [the age of] twenty-four.
Va.11.74 After that, they become those who have fallen from the <s>Sāvitrī</s> [initiation] (<s>patitasāvitrīka</s>).
Va.11.75 One should not initiate them, nor teach them, nor officiate at their sacrifices, nor should [one's daughters] be given in marriage to them.
Va.11.76 One who has fallen from the <s>Sāvitrī</s> should perform the <s>Uddālaka</s> observance.

body.text: Va.11.77 dvau māsau yāvakena vartayet(vṛt-)^māsam^payasā^ardha.māsam āmikṣayā^aṣṭa.rātram^ghṛtena ṣaṭ.rātram a.yācitena tri.rātram ab.bhakṣas^ahar.rātram upavaset(upa-vas-) //
body.translated_text: Va.11.77 For two months he should subsist on barley gruel; for one month on milk; for a half-month on <s>āmikṣā</s> (curdled milk); for eight nights on ghee; for six nights on unbegged food; for three nights without food; and for one day and night he should fast.
Va.11.78 He should go to the concluding bath of an <s>Aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifice).
Va.11.79 Or he should sacrifice with the <s>Vrātyastoma</s>. Or he should sacrifice. Thus it is said.
Va.12.1 Now, from this [point], the observances for the <s>Snātaka</s> (graduate).
Va.12.2 He should not beg from anyone, except from the king and his co-students.

body.text: Va.12.3 kṣudhā.parītas tu kim.cit^eva yāceta(yāc-) kṛtam akṛtam^vā kṣetram^gām aja.avikam antatas^hiraṇyam^dhānyam annam^vā //
body.translated_text: Va.12.3 But when afflicted by hunger, he may beg for something—whether prepared or unprepared—a field, a cow, a goat or sheep, or at the very least, gold, grain, or food.
Va.12.4 'A <s>Snātaka</s> should not waste away from hunger'—this is the teaching.
Va.12.5 He should not live together with one who wears soiled garments.
Va.12.6 Nor with a menstruating woman.
Va.12.7 Nor with an unsuitable woman.
Va.12.8 He should not be one who wanders from family to family.
Va.12.9 He should not step over a stretched rope for tethering a calf.
Va.12.10 He should not look at the rising sun nor at the setting sun.
Va.12.11 He should not urinate or defecate in water.
Va.12.12 He should not spit.

body.text: Va.12.13 pariveṣṭita.śirās^bhūmim ayajñiyais tṛṇais^antardhāya(antar-dhā-) mutra.purīṣe kuryāt(kṛ-)^udaṅ.mukhas^ca^ahani naktam^dakṣiṇā.mukhas^sandhyām āsīta(ās-)^uttaram //{BṣPṣ mutra.purīṣe}{F mūtra.purīṣe}
body.translated_text: Va.12.13 With his head wrapped, having covered the ground with non-sacrificial grass, he should urinate and defecate—facing north during the day, facing south at night; at twilight he should face north.
Va.12.14 And they also cite [the following]:
Va.12.14 A <s>Snātaka</s> should always have an undergarment and an upper garment,
Va.12.14 two sacred threads (<s>yajñopavīta</s>), a staff, and a water-pot (<s>kamaṇḍalu</s>) with water.

body.text: Va.12.15 apsu pāṇau ca kāṣṭhe ca kathitam^pāvake śucis^(c)/
body.translated_text: Va.12.15 In water, in the hand, and in wood—when [these are present along with] fire, one is pure.
Va.12.15 Therefore one should wipe the water-pot with water and hands.
Va.12.16 For this is [equivalent to] the circumambulation with fire—thus <s>Manu</s> <s>Prajāpati</s> has declared.
Va.12.17 And having performed the obligatory duties, the one most learned in purification should sip water (<s>ācamana</s>). Thus it is said.
Va.12.18 One should eat food facing east.
Va.12.19 In silence, with the thumb [included], one should swallow the morsel whole.
Va.12.20 And one should not make noise [while eating].
Va.12.21 He should approach his own wife during the proper season, avoiding the <s>parvan</s> (prohibited) days.
Va.12.22 He should not approach [her] in an unnatural manner.

body.text: Va.12.23 yas tu pāṇigṛhītāyās^āsye kurvīta(kṛ-) maithunam (c)/
body.translated_text: Va.12.23 One who performs sexual intercourse at the mouth of one whose hand has been taken [in marriage]—
Va.12.23 his ancestors subsist on his semen for that month.
Va.12.23 That sexual pleasure which is obtained through irregular conduct is connected with <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness).

body.text: Va.12.24 api ca kāṭhake vijñāyate(vi-jñā-) / api nas^śvas^vijaniṣyamāṇās(vi-jan-)^patibhis^saha śayīran(śī-)^iti strīṇām indra.dattas^varas^iti //
body.translated_text: Moreover, it is known in the <s>Kāṭhaka</s> [recension]: 'May even those women who will be born tomorrow lie with their husbands'—this boon was given to women by <s>Indra</s>.
One should not climb a tree.
One should not descend into a well.
One should not blow upon fire with the mouth.
One should not pass between a fire and a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.
Nor between two fires.
Nor between two <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, unless with [their] permission.
One should not eat together with one's wife—it is known from the <s>Vājasaneya</s> [recension]: 'the offspring becomes lacking in vigor.'
One should not refer to the rainbow by the name '<s>Indradhanus</s>' (Indra's bow).
One should say '<s>Maṇidhanus</s>' (jewel-bow).

body.text: Va.12.34 pālāśam āsanam^pāduke danta.dhāvanam iti varjayet(vṛj-) //
body.translated_text: One should avoid a seat made of <s>Palāśa</s> wood, shoes, and tooth-cleaning sticks [made from it].
One should not eat [with food] in one's lap.
One should not eat [while seated] on a couch.
One should carry a bamboo staff.
And gold earrings.
One should not wear an external garland, except one made of gold.
One should avoid assemblies and gatherings.
Moreover, they cite [the following]:
Denying the authority of the <s>Vedas</s>, and disparaging the seers (<s>ṛṣis</s>),

body.text: Va.12.41 a.vyavasthā ca sarvatra etat^nāśanam ātmanas.(c) iti //
body.translated_text: And lawlessness everywhere—this is the destruction of the self. Thus.
One who has not been invited should not go to a sacrifice; if he does go, he should circumambulate and return.
One should not undertake a journey when the sun is above the trees.
One should not board a doubtful boat.
One should not cross a river using one's arms [alone].
Having risen in the latter part of the night and having studied, one should not go back to sleep.
In the <s>Prājāpatya</s> <s>muhūrta</s> (the hour before dawn), a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should observe certain observances—should observe [them]. Thus.
Now, from here [begins] the commencement of <s>svādhyāya</s> (Vedic self-study), on the full moon day of <s>Śrāvaṇa</s> or of <s>Prauṣṭhapada</s> (Bhādrapada).
Having prepared the fire, one offers oblations of unbroken grains and parched grains,
To the gods, to the seers, and to the meters—thus.

body.text: Va.13.4 brāhmaṇān svasti.vācya(vāc-) dadhi prāśya(pra-aś-) tatas^adhyāyān upākurvīran(upa-ā-kṛ-) //
body.translated_text: Having had <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> pronounce blessings and having eaten curds, they should then commence the study sessions.
For four and a half months or five and a half months.
After that, one should study during the bright fortnights.
But the <s>Vedāṅgas</s> (auxiliary sciences of the <s>Veda</s>) may be [studied] at will.
The [following are] occasions for not studying (<s>anadhyāya</s>):
When there is thunder at the junctures [of day and night].
During the junctures [dawn and dusk].
In towns where there is a corpse within, during the daytime, and when [the names of towns] are being announced.
But [study is permissible] at will on ground purified with cow-dung or on ground that has been marked [with lines].
Near a cremation ground.
For one who is lying down.
For one who has [just] performed a funeral offering (<s>śrāddha</s>).
And here they cite a verse from <s>Manu</s>:
Fruits, water, sesame seeds, food, and whatever else pertains to a <s>śrāddha</s>—
Even after accepting [these], <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> are considered to be in a state of non-study [with] food in their hands [and mouths]. Thus.
