While running; in a place with a foul smell and the like; on barren land.
For one who has climbed a tree.
In a boat and in an army.
And after eating, while the hands are still wet.
When there is the sound of an arrow.
On the fourteenth [day of the fortnight], on the new-moon day, on the eighth, and on the <s>Aṣṭakā</s> days.
And for one who is sitting with legs stretched out or [leaning] against the genitals [i.e., in an improper posture].
In the proximity of the teacher.
On the [night] following sexual intercourse.
With a garment [that has been in contact with] sexual intercourse and that has not been washed.
At the outskirts of a village.
For one who has vomited.
For one who has urinated or defecated.
When the sound of <s>Sāman</s> [chanting is heard], while [studying] the <s>Ṛc</s> and <s>Yajus</s> [texts].
During indigestion.
During a loud thunderclap.
During an earthquake.
During an eclipse of the moon or sun.
During sounds from the sky, landslides, and showers of stones, blood, or dust—[the non-study is] untimely [i.e., lasts as long as the phenomenon].
In the case of a meteor or lightning, [non-study lasts] for three nights.
A meteor or lightning [occurring] with [other] celestial lights [—non-study lasts until the light ceases].
Outside the [regular Vedic study] season, [non-study is] untimely [i.e., circumstantial].
When the teacher dies, [non-study lasts] for three nights.
For the [death of] the teacher's son, pupil, or wife—[non-study lasts] for a day and a night.
One should rise and greet the sacrificial priest (<s>ṛtvij</s>), father-in-law, paternal uncle, and maternal uncle who are not younger [than oneself].

body.text: Va.13.42 ye ca^eva pāda.grāhyās teṣām^bhāryā guros^ca //
body.translated_text: And those whose feet are to be grasped—their wives [are also to be honored]; and [the wife] of the teacher.
And one's mother and father.

body.text: Va.13.44 yas^vidyāt(vid-)^abhivaditum(abhi-vad-) aham ayam^bho iti yāt //
body.translated_text: He who knows how to greet should say: 'I am so-and-so, sir'—thus he should go.
And he who does not know [the proper form].

body.text: Va.13.46 pratyabhivādam āmantrite svaras^antyas^plavate(plu-) sandhi.akṣaram a.pragṛhyam āya.āva.bhāvam^ca^āpadyate(ā-pad-) yathā bho bhāv iti //
body.translated_text: In the response to a greeting (<s>pratyabhivāda</s>), when addressed, the last vowel is lengthened, a juncture-letter [is formed], [the vowel] is not held separately (<s>apragṛhya</s>), and it takes the form of <s>āya</s>, <s>āva</s>, <s>bhāva</s>—for example, 'O <s>Bho</s>' becomes '<s>Bhāv</s>.'

body.text: Va.13.47 patitas^pitā parityājyas^mātā tu putre na patati(pat-) //
body.translated_text: A fallen father should be abandoned; but a mother does not fall with respect to her son.
Moreover, they cite [the following]:
Ten sub-teachers (<s>upādhyāya</s>) [equal one] teacher (<s>ācārya</s>); a hundred teachers [equal one] father;
A thousand [times] the father—the mother surpasses [all] in venerability.
A wife, sons, and pupils who are associated with sinful deeds—
Having admonished them, they should be abandoned; one who abandons a fallen [person] otherwise [i.e., without admonishing] falls [himself].
A sacrificial priest and a teacher who do not perform sacrifice or do not teach should be abandoned; apart from [proper] abandonment, one falls.
One born of a fallen [person] becomes fallen—so they say, except in the case of a woman.
For she is one who goes to another [i.e., belongs to the husband's family].
One should approach her without [giving her] inheritance.
When the teacher's teacher is present, one should behave toward him as toward the teacher;
And one should behave toward the teacher's son as toward the teacher—so says the <s>śruti</s> (scripture).
Weapons, poison, and liquor are not to be accepted by a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.
Learning, wealth, age, kinship, and [ritual] action are [grounds for] honor.
The earlier [in the list] is weightier than the subsequent.
When meeting on the road, the path should be given to the elderly, to the young [child], to the sick, to one carrying a load, to a woman, to one in a carriage—to each [successive] one.
When a king and a <s>snātaka</s> (graduate) meet, the king should give way to the <s>snātaka</s>.
All [should give way] to a bride being led [to the wedding].
Grass, space, fire, water, and kind and truthful speech free from envy—these are never cut off in the house of good people, never. Thus.
Now, from here we shall describe what is fit and unfit to eat.
The food of a physician, a hunter, a prostitute, a constable, a thief, one accused [of a crime], a eunuch, and a fallen person is not to be eaten.

[The food of] a miser, one who has undertaken a consecration (<s>dīkṣita</s>), one who is imprisoned, one who is sick, a <s>Soma</s>-seller, a carpenter, a washerman, a distiller, an informer, a usurer, and a leather-cutter [is not to be eaten].
And [the food] of a <s>Śūdra</s>.
And of one who bears arms.
And of a paramour, and of one who tolerates a paramour [in her household].
And of one who sets fire to houses.
And of one who does not punish those deserving punishment.
Food that has been publicly announced with 'Who will eat?'
Food of a guild, and food of a courtesan—thus.
Moreover, they cite [the following]:
The gods do not eat [the offerings] of one who keeps dogs, nor of one whose wife is a <s>Śūdra</s> woman;

body.text: Va.14.11 bhāryā.jitasya na^aśnanti(aś-) yasya ca^upapatis^gṛhe.(c) iti //
body.translated_text: Nor of one ruled by his wife, nor of one in whose house there is a paramour. Thus.
Fuel, water, fodder-grass, <s>kuśa</s> grass, parched grains, an offered vehicle, a dwelling-place, small fish, millet, garlands, perfumes, honey, and meat—of these one may accept.
Moreover, they cite [the following]:
For the sake of the teacher, for maintaining one's wife, and for worshipping gods and guests,

body.text: Va.14.13 sarvatas^pratigṛhṇīyāt(prati-grah-)^na tu tṛpyet(tṛp-) svayam^tatas.(c) iti //
body.translated_text: One may accept from all sources; but one should not indulge oneself thereby. Thus.
The food of a hunter who uses arrows is not to be avoided.

body.text: Va.14.15 vijñāyate(vi-jñā-) hi / agastyas^varṣa.sāhasrike satre mṛgayām^cacāra(car-) / tasya^a.saṃstara.samayās^puroḍāśās^mṛgapakṣiṇām^praśastānām //{BṣPṣ satre}{F sattre}
body.translated_text: For it is known: <s>Agastya</s>, during a thousand-year sacrificial session (<s>sattra</s>), went hunting; his sacrificial cakes were [made from the flesh] of praised wild animals and birds, without the use of a slaughtering block.
And here they cite verses attributed to <s>Prajāpati</s>:
Food that is offered spontaneously, that has been brought, that has been begged without prior prompting—
<s>Prajāpati</s> considered [this] to be fit to eat, even from an evildoer.
One should eat [the food] of one who is faithful, and especially of a thief [who offers with faith],

body.text: Va.14.17 na tu^eva bahu.yājyasya yas^ca^upanayate(upa-nī-) bahūn (c)//
body.translated_text: But not of one who sacrifices for many, nor of one who initiates many [students for gain].

body.text: Va.14.18 na tasya pitaras^aśnanti(aś-) daśa varṣāṇi pañca ca (c)/
body.translated_text: For fifteen years, his ancestors do not eat [his offerings],

body.text: Va.14.18 na ca havyam^vahati(vah-)^agnis^yas tām abhyavamanyate(abhi-ava-man-) (c)//
body.translated_text: Nor does the fire carry [his] oblation—[for] one who despises that [food offered with faith].
Of a physician, a hunter, a surgeon (remover of arrows), and a sinner,

body.text: Va.14.19 ṣaṇḍhasya kulaṭāyās^ca udyatā^api na gṛhyate(grah-).(c) iti //
body.translated_text: Of a eunuch, and of an unchaste woman—even food offered [by them] is not to be accepted. Thus.
The leavings (<s>ucchiṣṭa</s>) of one who is not a teacher are not to be eaten.
And one's own leavings, and what has been contaminated by [others'] leavings.
And what has been contaminated by cloth, hair, or insects.

body.text: Va.14.23 kāmam^tu keśa.kīṭān uddhṛtya(ud-hṛ-)^adbhis^prokṣya(pra-ukṣ-) bhasmanā^avakīrya(ava-kṝ-) vācā praśastam upayuñjīta(upa-yuj-) //
body.translated_text: But if one wishes, having removed the hair or insects, sprinkling with water, covering with ashes, and [having it] praised with speech, one may eat it.
And here they cite verses attributed to <s>Prajāpati</s>:
The gods ordained three purifiers for <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>:
What is unseen [by the eye], what is washed with water, and what is praised with speech.
In a <s>Devadroni</s> (divine trough/vessel), at weddings, and at ongoing sacrifices,

body.text: Va.14.25 kākais^śvabhis^ca saṃspṛṣṭam annam tat^na visarjayet(vi-sṛj-) (c)/
body.translated_text: Food that has been touched by crows or dogs—that food should not be discarded.
Having removed [the contaminated portion] from that food, the remainder deserves purification—
Liquids by dilution, and solids by sprinkling [with water].
What has been touched by the mouth of a cat is indeed pure.
Stale food, food that is spoiled in nature, food with furrows [drawn through it by hand], re-cooked food, raw meat and cooked [meat]—

body.text: Va.14.29 kāmam^tu dadhnā ghṛtena vā^abhighāritam upayuñjīta(upa-yuj-) //
body.translated_text: But if one wishes, one may eat [these] when moistened with curds or ghee.
And here they cite verses attributed to <s>Prajāpati</s>:
Va.14.30 Ghee or oil that has fallen from the nails—a learned <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should not eat [it].
Va.14.30 <s>Yama</s> has declared it impure, equal to eating cow's flesh.

body.text: Va.14.31 hasta.dattās tu ye snehās^lavaṇa.vyañjanāni ca (c)/
body.translated_text: Va.14.31 Oils and condiments with salt that are given by hand—
Va.14.31 they do not benefit the giver; the eater consumes sin.

body.text: Va.14.32 pradadyāt(pra-dā-)^ na tu hastena na^āyasena kadā.cana.(c) iti //
body.translated_text: Va.14.32 One should serve [them] not by hand, nor ever with an iron [vessel]. Thus it is said.

Va.14.33 For eating garlic, onion, <s>kyāku</s> (a type of plant), <s>gṛñjana</s> (a type of shallot), sap of the <s>śleṣmāntaka</s> tree, blood, flesh [obtained by] cutting, food left over by dogs, crows, or <s>Śūdras</s>—[the penance is] an <s>atikṛcchra</s> (severe penance).
Va.14.34 [One should not drink] the milk of a cow that has just calved (<s>sandhinī</s>), or of a cow that has no calf.
Va.14.35 [Likewise] of cows, buffaloes, and goats within ten days [of calving].
Va.14.36 [One should not drink] water from within a boat.

Va.14.37 One should avoid cakes, parched grain, <s>karambha</s> (barley gruel), <s>saktu</s> (flour), <s>vaṭaka</s> (fried balls), oil, rice pudding, vegetables, and fermented foods [when offered by unfit persons].
Va.14.38 And other preparations of milk, barley, and flour.
Va.14.39 Among five-clawed animals, the porcupine, hedgehog, hare, tortoise, and iguana (<s>godhā</s>) are edible.
Va.14.40 Among domestic animals, those that have teeth on one side only [are edible], excluding the camel.
Va.14.41 Among fish, the <s>ceṭa</s>, <s>gavaya</s> (wild ox-fish), porpoise (<s>śiśumāra</s>), crocodile (<s>nakra</s>), and crab are [not edible].
Va.14.42 [Also not edible are fish] of deformed appearance and those with snake-like heads.
Va.14.43 And the white ox (<s>gaura</s>), wild ox (<s>gavaya</s>), and <s>śarabha</s> (eight-legged mythical animal).
Va.14.44 Likewise, [animals] not specifically designated [for sacrifice are not to be eaten].
Va.14.45 And a milch cow and a bull, and those with broken teeth [are not to be eaten].

body.text: Va.14.46 bhakṣyau(bhakṣ-) tu dhenu.anaḍuhau medhyau vājasaneyake vijñāyate(vi-jñā-) //
body.translated_text: Va.14.46 But [according to] the <s>Vājasaneyins</s>, it is known that a milch cow and a bull are edible [if] fit for sacrifice (<s>medhya</s>).
Va.14.47 But there is dispute regarding the rhinoceros (<s>khaḍga</s>) and the wild boar.

Va.14.48 And among birds [the following are not edible]: the <s>viṣuviṣkara</s>, web-footed birds, the <s>kalaviṅka</s> (sparrow), the diver (<s>plava</s>), the <s>haṃsa</s> (goose/swan), the <s>cakravāka</s> (ruddy shelduck), the <s>bhāsa</s> (vulture), the crow (<s>vāyasa</s>), the pigeon (<s>pārāvata</s>), the osprey (<s>kurara</s>), the <s>sāraṅga</s>, the ash-colored pigeon (<s>pāṇḍukapota</s>), the heron (<s>krauñca</s>), the <s>krakara</s>, the <s>kaṅka</s> (heron), the vulture (<s>gṛdhra</s>), the hawk (<s>śyena</s>), the crane (<s>baka</s>), the white crane (<s>balāka</s>), the cormorant (<s>madgu</s>), the plover (<s>ṭiṭṭibha</s>), the <s>māndhāla</s>, nocturnal [birds] (<s>naktañcara</s>), the woodpecker (<s>dārvāghāṭa</s>), the <s>cakaṭa</s>, the <s>railātaka</s>, the <s>hārīta</s> (green pigeon), the wagtail (<s>khañjarīṭa</s>), the domestic fowl (<s>grāmyakukkuṭa</s>), the parrot (<s>śuka</s>), the <s>śārikā</s> (mynah), the cuckoo (<s>kokila</s>), carnivorous [birds], and those that frequent villages. Thus it is said.
Va.15.1 A person is born from the union of blood and semen, having the mother and father as his origin.
Va.15.2 The mother and father have authority over his gift, sale, and abandonment.
Va.15.3 But one should not give away or accept in adoption an only son.
Va.15.4 For he is [needed] for the continuation [of the line] of the forefathers.
Va.15.5 A woman should not give away or accept a son in adoption without the permission of her husband.

body.text: Va.15.6 putram^pratigṛhīṣyan(prati-grah-) bandhūn āhūya(ā-hū-) rājani ca nivedya(ni-vid-) niveśanasya madhye vyāhṛtibhis^hutvā(hu-)^adūra.bāndhavam^bandhu.sannikṛṣṭam eva pratigṛhṇīyāt(prati-grah-) //
body.translated_text: Va.15.6 One who intends to accept a son in adoption, having summoned the relatives and having informed the king, should, in the middle of the dwelling, having offered oblations with the <s>Vyāhṛtis</s> (sacred exclamations), accept [in adoption] one who is not distantly related, one who is closely related to kinsmen.

body.text: Va.15.7 sandehe ca^utpanne dūre.bāndhavam^śūdram iva sthāpayet(sthā-) //
body.translated_text: Va.15.7 And if doubt arises [about a near relative], one who is distantly related should be appointed like a <s>Śūdra</s> [i.e., without full ritual rights].
Va.15.8 For it is known [in the scriptures]: 'By one, many are saved.'
Va.15.9 If, after the adopted son has been accepted, a natural son (<s>aurasa</s>) is born, the adopted son (<s>dattaka</s>) shall receive a one-fourth share.
Va.15.10 Provided he is not employed in auspicious [family] rites.

Va.15.11 Those who pervert the <s>Vedas</s>, who sacrifice for <s>Śūdras</s>, and those fallen from the group of the highest <s>varṇa</s>—for them, the removal of the [ritual] vessel [is the punishment].

body.text: Va.15.12 a.pātra.saṅkarāt^a.kṛtsnam^pātram ādāya(ā-dā-) dāsas^a.savarṇā.putras^vā bandhus^a.sadṛśas^vā guṇa.hīnas^savyena pādena pravṛtta.agrān darbhān^lohitān vā^upastīrya(upa-stṝ-) pūrṇa.pātram asmai ninayet(ni-nī-) //
body.translated_text: Va.15.12 In order to avoid the mixing of [fit and] unfit vessels, a slave or the son of a wife of unequal <s>varṇa</s>, or a kinsman of dissimilar [status], or one deficient in qualities, should take a full vessel not completely [filled], having spread beneath it <s>darbha</s> grass with the tips pointing forward, or red [grass], with the left foot, and should remove it for him.
Va.15.13 And his kinsmen, with disheveled hair, should touch the one who removes [the vessel].
Va.15.14 Having performed the reverse circumambulation, they should freely return to their houses.
Va.15.15 From that [time] onward, they should not maintain him in [righteous] observances.
Va.15.16 [But] those who follow his observances [share his punishment] by maintaining him in [those] observances.
Va.15.17 But for the fallen who have performed their penances, there is restoration.
Va.15.18 And they also cite [the following]:
Va.15.18 He should approach those who restore [the fallen] first, as if playing, as if laughing.
Va.15.18 He should approach those who cause [one] to fall afterward, as if grieving, as if weeping. Thus it is said.
Va.15.19 Those who have killed a teacher, mother, or father—[they may be restored] by the favor of those [offended], or [those offended] may send them away. This is their restoration.

body.text: Va.15.20 puṇya.hradāt prasṛtāt^vā kāñcanam^pātram^māheyam^vā pūrayitvā^āpas.hi.ṣṭhābhis^enam adbhis^abhiṣiñcanti(abhi-sic-) //(cf^.9.1 obhtūrjhātana / mahṇāya ce //)
body.translated_text: Va.15.20 Having filled a golden vessel or one made of buffalo horn with water from a sacred pool or from a flowing [stream], they consecrate him by sprinkling with waters [accompanied by the <s>Āpohiṣṭhā</s> hymn].
Va.15.21 The restoration of everyone who has been thus consecrated is explained as [equivalent to the restoration that comes] by the birth of a son. Thus it is explained.
Va.16.1 Now, [the rules of] legal procedure (<s>vyavahāra</s>).

body.text: Va.16.2 rājā mantrī vā sadas.kāryāṇi kuryāt(kṛ-) //
body.translated_text: Va.16.2 The king or his minister should adjudicate the matters of the court.
Va.16.3 Of two disputants, he should not go to the side of either.
Va.16.4 [He should deal with offenses] according to their gravity; an offense is [to be assessed] by its conclusion.
Va.16.5 Being equal toward all beings, [he should deal] according to the gravity of the offense; for the first two <s>varṇas</s>, [the assessment should also be] based on learning.
Va.16.6 And he should protect what has been accomplished.
Va.16.7 [He should protect] the property of the king and of minors.
Va.16.8 Of those who have not reached the age of legal competence.
Va.16.9 But when the time has arrived, [he should hand over] that which [is theirs].
Va.16.10 Written documents, witnesses, and possession—evidence is remembered as threefold.
Va.16.10 The recovery of property [is] first; the owner should obtain his property. Thus it is said.

body.text: Va.16.11 mārga.kṣetrebhyas^visargas tathā parivarttanam //{BṣPṣ parivarttanam}{F parivartanam}
body.translated_text: Va.16.11 From roads and fields, there should be release [of encroachments] and likewise exchange.
Va.16.12 For newly [built] houses and other matters, [the boundary is] only three footsteps.
Va.16.13 In a dispute about a house or field, [the decision rests on] the testimony of neighbors.
Va.16.14 In a dispute among neighbors, [the decision rests on] the written document.
Va.16.15 In a dispute about the written document, [the decision rests on] the testimony of village elders, town elders, or guild leaders.
Va.16.16 And they also cite [the following]:

body.text:
Va.16.16 paitṛkam^krītam ādheyam anvādheyam^pratigraham (c)/
Va.16.16 yajñāt^upagamas^veṇis tathā dhūma.śikhā^aṣṭamī.(c) iti //
body.translated_text: Va.16.16 Paternal [property], purchased [property], pledged property, subsequent gifts, received gifts, [property obtained] from sacrifice, acquisition, inherited property (<s>veṇi</s>), and [property received as] smoke-offering (<s>dhūmaśikhā</s>)—[these are] the eight [types of property]. Thus it is said.
Va.16.17 Therein, [the rule of] possession [applies when the property has been] enjoyed and used for ten years.
Va.16.18 Others also cite differently:
Va.16.18 A pledge, a boundary, the property of a minor, a deposit, an entrustment, women,
Va.16.18 the king's property, and a learned <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>'s property—these are not lost through [another's] enjoyment.
Va.16.19 Properties [whose owners] have perished go to the king.

body.text: Va.16.20 tatas^anyathā rājā mantribhis^saha nāgarais^ca kāryāṇi kuryāt(kṛ-) //
body.translated_text: Va.16.20 In other cases, the king should adjudicate matters together with the ministers and townspeople.
Va.16.21 A king who has a discerning [council] is better; [better still] would be one with a vulture-like retinue [i.e., watchful advisors].
Va.16.22 Or a king with a vulture-like retinue is better.
Va.16.23 [A king] should have a vulture-like retinue, but should not be a vulture [himself] with a vulture-like retinue.
Va.16.24 For faults arise from the retinue.
Va.16.25 And [this leads to] theft, robbery, and destruction.
Va.16.26 Therefore, one should first examine the retinue.
Va.16.27 Now, [the rules regarding] witnesses.
Va.16.28 Those learned in the <s>Vedas</s>, of good appearance, of good character, virtuous, and truthful [should be] witnesses.
Va.16.29 Or in all [cases], anyone at all [may be a witness].
Va.16.30 For women, he should appoint women as witnesses; for the twice-born, similar twice-born; for <s>Śūdras</s>, virtuous <s>Śūdras</s>; and for the lowest [castes], those of lowest birth.
Va.16.31 And they also cite [the following]:
Va.16.31 A surety, a frivolous gift, a gambling [debt], and a liquor [debt]—
Va.16.31 and what remains after a fine or tax—the son does not inherit [the liability] of the giver.

body.text: Va.16.32 brūhi(brū-) sākṣin yathā.tattvam^lambante(lamb-) pitaras tava (c)/
body.translated_text: Va.16.32 'Speak, O witness, according to the truth—your ancestors are hanging [in the balance].'

body.text: Va.16.32 tava vākyam udīkṣāṇās(ud-īkṣ-)^utpatanti(ud-pat-) patanti(pat-) ca (c)//
body.translated_text: Va.16.32 'Watching for your word, they rise up and fall down.'
Va.16.33 Naked, shaven, carrying a skull-bowl, seeking alms, afflicted by hunger and thirst,
Va.16.33 blind, he shall go to the family of his enemy—one who speaks false testimony.

body.text: Va.16.34 pañca kanyā.anṛte hanti(han-) daśa hanti(han-) gava.anṛte (c)/
body.translated_text: Va.16.34 [False testimony] destroys five [persons] in a case involving a maiden; it destroys ten in a case involving cattle.
Va.16.34 It destroys a hundred in a case involving horses; it destroys a thousand in a case involving a person.
Va.16.35 In a legal proceeding [concerning] a deceased wife, the penance for a woman of [good] family—
Va.16.35 is cut off by the opponents through the prior adjudication of those [matters].
Va.16.36 At the time of marriage, in sexual union, when life is at stake, and when all wealth is being stolen—
Va.16.36 in the interest of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, one may speak falsehood. They say that these five falsehoods are not sinful.

body.text: Va.16.37 sva.jana.sva.arthe yadi vā^artha.hetos^pakṣa.āśrayeṇa^eva vadanti(vad-) kāryam (c)/
body.translated_text: Va.16.37 Those who speak in a case [motivated by] their own people, their own interest, or for the sake of wealth, out of partisanship—

body.text: Va.16.37 te śabda.vaṃśasya kulasya pūrvān svarga.sthitān^tān api pātayanti(pat-) (c)//
body.translated_text: Va.16.37 they cause even those ancestors of their family and lineage who are established in heaven to fall.
Va.16.37 They cause them to fall. Thus it is said.
Va.17.1 He repays the debt and attains immortality—
Va.17.1 the father, if he sees the face of a son born alive.
Va.17.2 'The worlds of those with sons are infinite; for one without a son, there is no world.' Thus it is heard [in the scriptures].
Va.17.3 'May those who harm us be without offspring'—this is an imprecation [from the <s>Ṛgveda</s>].

body.text: Va.17.4 prajābhis^agne amṛta.tvam aśyām iti^api nigamas^bhavati(bhū-) //(cf^ṛV.<5.004.10c> jātavedo yaśo asmāsu dhehi prajābhir agne amṛtatvam aśyām ||)
body.translated_text: Va.17.4 'Through offspring, O <s>Agni</s>, may I attain immortality'—this too is a Vedic statement.
Va.17.5 'By a son one conquers the worlds; by a grandson one attains infinity;

body.text: Va.17.5 atha putrasya pautreṇa bradhnasya^āpnoti(āp-) viṣṭapam(c) iti //
body.translated_text: Va.17.5 and by the grandson of a son, one reaches the realm of <s>Bradhna</s> (the Sun).' Thus it is said.
Va.17.6 [Whether] the son belongs to the field-owner (<s>kṣetrin</s>) or to the begetter (<s>janayitṛ</s>)—on this they disagree.
Va.17.7 There, on both sides, they also cite [authorities]:
Va.17.8 'If a bull in other [men's] cows should beget a hundred calves,

body.text: Va.17.8 gominām eva te vatsās^mogham^syanditam ārṣabham(c) iti //
body.translated_text: Va.17.8 those calves belong to the owners of the cows; the bull's semen is shed in vain.' Thus it is said.

body.text: Va.17.9 apramattās^rakṣata(rakṣ-) tantum etam^mā vas^kṣetre para.bījāni vāpsus(vap-)^/ janayitus^putras^bhavati(bhū-) saṃparāye mogham^tettā kurute(kṛ-) tantum etam iti //{BṣPṣ tettā}{E vettā}
body.translated_text: Va.17.9 'Watch carefully and protect this thread [of lineage]! Let not the seeds of others be sown in your field! The son belongs to the begetter in the next world; the one [who sows another's seed] renders this thread fruitless.' Thus it is said.

body.text: Va.17.10 bahūnām eka.jātānām ekas^cet putravān naras^(c)/
body.translated_text: Va.17.10 'Of many born together, if one man has a son,

body.text: Va.17.10 sarve te tena putreṇa putravantas^iti śrutis^(c)//
body.translated_text: Va.17.10 all of them, by that son, become possessors of sons.' Thus says the <s>Śruti</s>.

body.text: Va.17.11 bahvīnām eka.patnīnām ekā putravatī yadi (c)/
body.translated_text: Va.17.11 'Of many co-wives, if one has a son,

body.text: Va.17.11 sarvās tās tena putreṇa putravantyas^iti śrutis^(c)//
body.translated_text: Va.17.11 all of them, by that son, become possessors of sons.' Thus says the <s>Śruti</s>.
(Va.17.12) Twelve indeed are the types of sons recognized in the ancient texts.
(Va.17.13) The first is one begotten by oneself on one's own field (wife) who has been [properly] consecrated.
(Va.17.14) In the absence of such [a son], the second is one born of the field (wife) who has been appointed [to levirate] (<s>kṣetraja</s>).
(Va.17.15) The third is the daughter appointed [as a son] (<s>putrikā</s>).

body.text: Va.17.16 vijñāyate(vi-jñā-)^a.bhrātṛkā puṃsas^pitṝn abhyeti(abhi-i-) pratīcīnam^gacchati(gam-) putra.tvam //
body.translated_text: (Va.17.16) It is recognized [by scripture]: 'A girl without brothers goes backward [i.e., in reverse lineage] to her father's ancestors; she attains the status of a son.'
(Va.17.17) On this point, [there is] a verse:
(Va.17.17) 'I will give to you a maiden without brothers, adorned [for marriage];
(Va.17.17) The son who is born from her shall be my son' — thus.
(Va.17.18) The fourth is the son of a remarried woman (<s>paunarbhava</s>).

body.text: Va.17.19 yā kaumāram^bharttāram uttsṛjya(ud-sṛj-)^anyais^saha caritvā(car-) tasya^eva kuṭumbam āśrayati(ā-śri-) sā punar.bhūs^bhavati(bhū-) //{BṣPṣ bharttāram}{F bhartāram}{BṣPṣ uttsṛjya}{F utsṛjya}
body.translated_text: (Va.17.19) A woman who, having abandoned her husband from her youth, having lived with others, returns to his very household — she becomes a 'remarried woman' (<s>punarbhū</s>).

body.text: Va.17.20 yā ca klībam^patitam unmattam^vā bharttāram utsṛjya(ud-sṛj-)^anyam^patim^vindate(vid-) mṛte vā sā punar.bhūs^bhavati(bhū-) //{BṣPṣ bharttāram}{F bhartāram}
body.translated_text: (Va.17.20) And a woman who, having abandoned a husband who is impotent, fallen [from caste], or insane, finds another husband, or [does so] when he has died — she becomes a 'remarried woman' (<s>punarbhū</s>).
(Va.17.21) The fifth is the son born to an unmarried girl (<s>kānīna</s>).
(Va.17.22) [The son] whom an unconsecrated [girl] begets out of desire in her father's house — they say he becomes the son of the maternal grandfather.
(Va.17.23) And moreover they cite:

body.text: Va.17.23 aprattā duhitā yasya putram^vindeta(vid-) tulyatas^(c)/
body.translated_text: (Va.17.23) Whose unmarried daughter should obtain a son from an equal [in caste],

body.text: Va.17.23 putrī mātāmahas tena dadyāt(dā-) piṇḍam^haret(hṛ-)^dhanam(c) iti //
body.translated_text: (Va.17.23) By that [grandson] the maternal grandfather becomes one who has a son; he should give the funeral offering and take the wealth. Thus.
(Va.17.24) The sixth is one secretly born in the house (<s>gūḍhotpanna</s>).
(Va.17.25) Thus, these [six] are heirs, kinsmen, and rescuers from great fear — so they say.
(Va.17.26) Now, among [the sons who are] not heirs [nor] kinsmen, the first is the one received together [with the bride] (<s>sahoḍha</s>).
(Va.17.27) A woman who is married while pregnant — her son becomes a <s>sahoḍha</s> (received together [with the bride]).
(Va.17.28) The second is the adopted son (<s>dattaka</s>).
(Va.17.29) [He is one] whom both mother and father give [in adoption].
(Va.17.30) The third is the purchased son (<s>krīta</s>).
(Va.17.31) That is explained by [the story of] <s>Śunaḥśepa</s>.
(Va.17.32) King <s>Hariścandra</s> indeed purchased the son of <s>Ajīgarta Sauyavasi</s>.
(Va.17.33) The fourth is one who comes of his own accord (<s>svayam upāgata</s>).
(Va.17.34) That is explained by [the story of] <s>Śunaḥśepa</s>.

body.text: Va.17.35 śunaḥśepas^vai yūpe niyuktas^devatās tuṣṭāva(stu-) / tasya^iha devatās^pāśam^vimumucus(vi-muc-) tam ṛtvijas^ūcus(vac-)^/ mama^eva^ayam^putras^astu(as-)^iti tān ha na saṃpede(sam-pad-) / te saṃpādayāmāsus(sam-pad-)^/ eṣas^eva yam^kāmayet(kam-) tasya putras^astu(as-)^iti / tasya ha viśvāmitras^hotā^āsīt(as-) tasya putratvam iyāya(i-) //
body.translated_text: (Va.17.35) <s>Śunaḥśepa</s> indeed, having been bound to the sacrificial post, praised the gods. The gods released his bonds. The priests said: 'Let this [boy] be my son.' He did not agree with them. They settled [the matter thus]: 'Let him be the son of whomever he chooses.' Now <s>Viśvāmitra</s> was his <s>hotṛ</s> (chief priest) — [and so Śunaḥśepa] attained sonship with him.
(Va.17.36) The fifth is the abandoned [son] (<s>apaviddha</s>).
(Va.17.37) [He is one] whom, having been cast away by mother and father, one takes in.
(Va.17.38) The sixth is the son of a <s>Śūdra</s> [woman] — so they say. These are [the sons who are] not heirs [nor] kinsmen.
(Va.17.39) And moreover they cite:

body.text: Va.17.39 yasya pūrveṣām^ṣaṇṇām^na kas.cit^dāyādas^syāt(as-)^ete tasya dāyam^hareran(hṛ-)^iti //
body.translated_text: (Va.17.39) For one who has no heir among the first six — these [latter six] shall take his inheritance. Thus.
(Va.17.40) Now, the division of inheritance among brothers.
(Va.17.41) And [the shares of] those [wives] who are childless — [their shares remain with the brothers] until [those wives] obtain sons.
(Va.17.42) The eldest should take a double share.
(Va.17.43) And [an extra share of] every tenth [animal] of the cattle and horses.
(Va.17.44) The goats, sheep, and the house [go] to the youngest.
(Va.17.45) Iron [implements] and household utensils [go] to the middle [brother].
(Va.17.46) The women should divide the mother's bridal property.
(Va.17.47) If a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> has sons by <s>Brāhmaṇī</s>, <s>Kṣatriyā</s>, and <s>Vaiśyā</s> [wives],
(Va.17.48) The son of the <s>Brāhmaṇī</s> should take a triple share.
(Va.17.49) The son of the <s>Rājanyā</s> (Kṣatriyā) [should take] a double share.
(Va.17.50) The others should divide equally.

body.text: Va.17.51 yena ca^eṣām^svayam utpāditam^syāt(as-)^dvi.aṃśam eva haret(hṛ-) //
body.translated_text: (Va.17.51) And whatever has been self-earned by any one of them — he should take a double share of that alone.
(Va.17.52) But those who have entered another <s>āśrama</s> (stage of life) are without a share.
(Va.17.53) And also the impotent, the insane, and the fallen (outcastes).
(Va.17.54) [But there shall be] maintenance for the impotent and the insane.
(Va.17.55) The wife of a deceased [husband] should observe a vow for six months, eating [food] without alkali or salt, and should sleep on the ground.

body.text: Va.17.56 ūrdhvam^ṣaḍbhyas^māsebhyas^snāttvā śrāddham^ca patye dattvā(dā-) vidyā.karma.guru.yoni.saṃbandhān saṃnipātya(sam-ni-pat-) pitā bhrātā vā niyogam^kārayet(kṛ-) //{BṣPṣ snāttvā}{F snātvā}
body.translated_text: (Va.17.56) After six months, having bathed and having offered the <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral rite) to her husband, the father or brother should convene [relatives connected by] learning, [ritual] action, teacher, family, and kinship, and should arrange the appointment (<s>niyoga</s>).
(Va.17.57) One should not appoint [to levirate] a woman who is insane, unwilling, or diseased.
(Va.17.58) Nor [a woman who is] older [than the appointed man].
(Va.17.59) [The waiting period shall last up to] sixteen years.
(Va.17.60) Provided [the husband] is not afflicted by illness.

body.text: Va.17.61 prajāpatye muhūrte pāṇigrāhavat^upacaret(car-)^anyatra samprahāsya(sam-pra-has-) vāc.pāruṣya.daṇḍa.pāruṣyāt^ca //
body.translated_text: (Va.17.61) At the <s>muhūrta</s> (auspicious moment) sacred to <s>Prajāpati</s>, [the appointed man] should approach [her] as would a husband, except for jesting, harsh speech, and physical violence.
(Va.17.62) In [matters of] food, clothing, bathing, and anointing, [the wife] should have priority.
(Va.17.63) A [son] born to a woman who has not been appointed [to levirate] becomes the son of the begetter — so they say.
(Va.17.64) [But] if [she has been] appointed, [the son belongs] to the appointor.
(Va.17.65) There is no appointment (<s>niyoga</s>) [motivated merely] by greed for inheritance.
(Va.17.66) Or one should appoint [the levirate] after prescribing an expiation — so say some.
(Va.17.67) A maiden who has reached puberty should wait for three years.
(Va.17.68) After three years, she may find a husband of equal [status].
(Va.17.69) And moreover they cite:

body.text: Va.17.69 pitus^pramādāt tu yadi^iha kanyā vayas.pramāṇam^samatītya(sam-ati-i-) dīyate(dā-) (c)/
body.translated_text: (Va.17.69) If, through the father's negligence, a maiden here is given [in marriage] having exceeded the [proper] measure of age,

body.text: Va.17.69 sā hanti(han-) dātāram udīkṣamāṇā(ud-īkṣ-) kāla.atiriktā guru.dakṣiṇā^iva (c)//
body.translated_text: (Va.17.69) She destroys the giver while waiting, like a tutor's fee that has exceeded [its] time.
(Va.17.70) A father should give [in marriage] a maiden who is still unclothed [i.e., before puberty], out of fear of the [onset of her] menstrual period;
(Va.17.70) For when [a maiden] remains [unmarried while] menstruating, the sin reaches the father.
(Va.17.71) As many menstrual periods as touch a maiden who is willing and being sought [in marriage] by equals,

body.text: Va.17.71 bhrūṇāni tāvanti hatāni tābhyām^mātā.pitṛbhyām iti dharma.vādas^(c)//
body.translated_text: (Va.17.71) That many embryos are slain by those two — the mother and the father — such is the declaration of <s>dharma</s>.
(Va.17.72) If, when [a maiden] has been given [merely] with water and words, the bridegroom should die first,

body.text: Va.17.72 na ca mantra.upanītā syāt(as-) kumārī pitus^eva sā (c)//
body.translated_text: (Va.17.72) And she has not been led [through the marriage rites] with mantras — that maiden belongs to her father alone.

body.text: Va.17.73 balāt^cet prahṛtā kanyā mantrais^yadi na saṃskṛtā (c)/
body.translated_text: (Va.17.73) If a maiden has been seized by force and has not been consecrated with mantras,

body.text: Va.17.73 anyasmai vidhivat^deyā yathā kanyā tathā^eva sā (c)//
body.translated_text: (Va.17.73) She should be given to another according to the [proper] rite — she is just as [much] a maiden [as before].
(Va.17.74) When the bridegroom has died, [if] the girl has been consecrated only with mantras,

body.text: Va.17.74 sā cet^akṣata.yonis^syāt(as-) punas^saṃskāram arhati(arh-).(c) iti //
body.translated_text: (Va.17.74) If she is still a virgin (one whose womb is intact), she is eligible for re-consecration. Thus.
(Va.17.75) The wife of one who has gone abroad should wait for five years.
(Va.17.76) After five years, she should go to [the presence of] her husband.
(Va.17.77) If she is not favorably disposed toward the sojourn [of her husband who has gone abroad] for [the sake of] <s>dharma</s> and <s>artha</s>, she should conduct herself as if he were dead.

body.text: Va.17.78 evam^brāhmaṇī pañca prajātā^aprajātā catvāri rājanyā prajātā pañca^aprajātā trīṇi vaiśyā prajātā catvāri^aprajātā dve śūdrā prajātā trīṇi^aprajātā^ekam //
body.translated_text: (Va.17.78) Thus, a <s>Brāhmaṇī</s> [should wait] five [years if she has] borne children, four if childless; a <s>Rājanyā</s> (Kṣatriyā) [should wait] five [years] with children, three without; a <s>Vaiśyā</s> [should wait] four [years] with children, two without; a <s>Śūdrā</s> [should wait] three [years] with children, one without.
(Va.17.79) Beyond that [limit], among those who share the same property, birth, funeral offering, water [libation], and lineage — each prior [kinsman] has greater [authority].

body.text: Va.17.80 na tu khalu kulīne vidyamāne(vid-) paragāminī syāt(as-) //
body.translated_text: (Va.17.80) But indeed, when a man of [good] family is available, [the wife] should not go to another.

body.text: Va.17.81 yasya pūrveṣām^ṣaṇṇām^na kas.cit^dāyādas^syāt(as-) sapiṇḍās^putra.sthānīyās vā tasya dhanam^vibhajeran(vi-bhaj-) //
body.translated_text: (Va.17.81) When one has no heir among the first six [types of sons], the <s>sapiṇḍas</s> (paternal kinsmen) or those standing in the place of a son should divide his wealth.
(Va.17.82) In the absence of such [persons], the teacher and the pupil should take [the property].
(Va.17.83) In the absence of those two, the king should take [it].

body.text: Va.17.84 na tu brāhmaṇasya rājā haret(hṛ-) //
body.translated_text: (Va.17.84) But the king should not take [the property] of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.
(Va.17.85) The property of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is indeed terrible poison.

body.text: Va.17.86 na viṣam^viṣam iti^āhur(ah-) brahma.svam^viṣam ucyate(vac-) (c)/
body.translated_text: (Va.17.86) Poison is not [truly called] poison, they say — the property of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is [what is truly] called poison;
(Va.17.86) Poison kills only one person, [but] the property of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [destroys] sons and grandsons. Thus.
(Va.17.87) One should distribute [it] to virtuous men versed in the three <s>Vedas</s> — one should distribute [it]. Thus.
(Va.18.1) A [son] born of a <s>Brāhmaṇī</s> by a <s>Śūdra</s> becomes a <s>Caṇḍāla</s> — so they say.
(Va.18.2) [A son born of] a <s>Rājanyā</s> (Kṣatriyā) [by a Śūdra becomes] a <s>Vaiṇa</s>.
(Va.18.3) [A son born of] a <s>Vaiśyā</s> [by a Śūdra becomes] an <s>Antyāvasāyī</s>.
(Va.18.4) A [son] born of a <s>Brāhmaṇī</s> by a <s>Vaiśya</s> becomes a <s>Rāmaka</s> — so they say.
(Va.18.5) [A son born of] a <s>Rājanyā</s> [by a Vaiśya becomes] a <s>Pulkasa</s>.
(Va.18.6) A [son] born of a <s>Brāhmaṇī</s> by a <s>Rājanya</s> (Kṣatriya) becomes a <s>Sūta</s> — so they say.
(Va.18.7) And moreover they cite:
(Va.18.7) And those who are born in secret, who partake of the quality of reverse [caste] mixture (<s>pratiloma</s>),

body.text: Va.18.7c guṇa.ācāra.paribhraṃśāt karmabhis tān vijānīyus(vi-jñā-).(c) iti //
body.translated_text: (Va.18.7) One should recognize them by their actions, through the deterioration of [their] qualities and conduct. Thus.

(Va.18.8) Those born of women [separated by] one, two, or three [caste] intervals from <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>Kṣatriya</s>, and <s>Vaiśya</s> [men] become <s>Ambaṣṭha</s>, <s>Ugra</s>, and <s>Niṣāda</s> [respectively].
(Va.18.9) For <s>Śūdras</s>, [the sons of Brāhmaṇas by Śūdra women are called] <s>Pāraśavas</s>.
(Va.18.10) A <s>Pāraśava</s> — [the name means] 'one who, though living, is indeed a corpse' — so they say.
(Va.18.11) Some say: 'They who are <s>Śūdras</s> are indeed a cremation ground.'
(Va.18.12) Therefore, one should not study [the <s>Veda</s>] in the vicinity of a <s>Śūdra</s>.
(Va.18.13) And moreover they cite verses sung by <s>Yama</s>:
(Va.18.13) 'Those <s>Śūdras</s> who are of sinful conduct are a visible cremation ground;
(Va.18.13) Therefore, one should never study [the <s>Veda</s>] in the vicinity of a <s>Śūdra</s>.'
(Va.18.14) 'One should not give counsel to a <s>Śūdra</s>, nor leftover food, nor offerings prepared with <s>havis</s> (oblation);

body.text: Va.18.14b na ca^asya^upadiśet(upa-diś-)^dharmam^na ca^asya vratam ādiśet(ā-diś-) (c)//
body.translated_text: (Va.18.14) Nor should one teach him <s>dharma</s>, nor prescribe a vow for him.'
(Va.18.15) 'He who teaches him <s>dharma</s> and he who prescribes a vow for him —

body.text: Va.18.15 sas^asaṃvṛttam^tamas^ghoram^saha tena prapadyate(pra-pad-).(c) iti //{BṣPṣ asaṃvṛttam}{F asaṃvṛtam}
body.translated_text: (Va.18.15) He enters, together with that [<s>Śūdra</s>], into terrible, unending darkness.' Thus.
(Va.18.16) If a worm should ever arise at the opening of a wound,
(Va.18.16) One is purified by [performing] the <s>Prājāpatya</s> [penance]; gold, a cow, and a garment are the gifts. Thus.
(Va.18.17) Having established the [sacred] fires, one should not approach a woman [merely for pleasure].

body.text: Va.18.18 kṛṣṇa.varṇā yā rāmā ramaṇāya^eva na dharmāya na dharmāya^iti //
body.translated_text: (Va.18.18) A dark-complexioned woman who is pleasing — [she is] for enjoyment only, not for <s>dharma</s>, not for <s>dharma</s>. Thus.
(Va.19.1) The own duty (<s>svadharma</s>) of a king is the protection of [all] beings; by its performance [comes] success.

body.text: Va.19.2 bhaya.kāruṇya.hānam^jarā.maryam^vai^etat satttram āhur(ah-) vidvāṃsas(vid-)^//{BṣPṣ satttram}{F sattram}
body.translated_text: (Va.19.2) Abandonment of fear and pity, having old age as the [only] boundary — the learned call this the [lifelong] sacrificial session (<s>sattra</s>).
(Va.19.3) Therefore, for the regular duties of the householder, one should appoint a family priest (<s>purohita</s>).
It is known: 'A kingdom with <s>Brahman</s> as its priest prospers.'
Because of the protection of both [king and priest].
And because of [their mutual] capability.

body.text: Va.19.7 deśa.dharma.jāti.kula.dharmān sarvān eva^etān anupraviśya(anu-pra-viś-) rājā caturas^varṇān sva.dharme sthāpayet(sthā-) //
body.translated_text: Having entered into all the customs of the region, the customs of <s>dharma</s>, of caste, and of family, the king should establish the four <s>varṇas</s> (classes) in their own duties.
When they transgress, he should impose punishment.
Punishment, however, should be determined according to the particulars of region, time, law, age, learning, and position, in cases of injury and verbal abuse.
Based on scripture and on observed precedent.
One should not harm trees that bear flowers and fruit.
But one may cut them down for the purpose of cultivation.
The measures and weights pertaining to household affairs should be protected [by the king].
There should be no removal of one's own goods from the place of storage.
The export duty should be only the value of the measure [i.e., a standard fee].
On highways between great markets, there should be a road.
In a caravan, a ten-cart train should carry double loads.
Each [halting place] should have drinking-water stations.
And one should summon [for labor] men of no less than a hundred [in number], half [being the minimum].
Women should not be idle [i.e., should be employed usefully].
A <s>karāṣṭhīlā</s> (small copper coin) is a <s>māṣa</s>; a <s>śaramadhyāpa</s> is a <s>pāda</s> (quarter); these are the <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> (standard currency units).
A waterless [ferry] crossing may be charged a toll.
Exempt from tax are: a <s>Śrotriya</s> (learned Brahmin), a king's servant, the unprotected, the renunciant, a child, the aged, a young woman, and one who has just given birth.
Also exempt are maidens going [to their husband's house], and women whose [travel] expenses are paid.
One who [takes tolls] by force beyond [what is prescribed] should pay a hundredfold.
The use of rivers, thickets, forests, [areas destroyed by] fire, and mountains should be free of tax.
Or those who subsist on them should pay [the tax].
He should collect the marriage tax monthly.

body.text: Va.19.29 rājani ca prete(pra-i-) dadyāt(dā-) prāsaṅgikam //
body.translated_text: And when the king dies, he should give the customary [funeral offerings].
By this, the maternal duty [of the king toward his subjects] is explained.
The king should maintain the paternal uncles and maternal uncles of the chief queen.
And their relatives and others as well.
The king's wives should receive food and clothing.
Or, if unwilling [to remain], they may renounce [and become ascetics].
The king should maintain the impotent and the insane.
Because the inheritance goes to him [the king, in their case].
And regarding tolls, they cite a verse from <s>Manu</s>:

body.text: Va.19.37 na bhinna.kārṣāpaṇam asti(as-) śulke na śilpa.vṛttas^na śiśau na dūte (c)/
body.translated_text: There is no toll on a broken <s>kārṣāpaṇa</s>, nor on one who lives by crafts, nor on a child, nor on a messenger,

body.text: Va.19.37 na bhaikṣa.labdhe na hṛta.avaśeṣe na śrotriye pravrajite na yajñe.(c) iti //
body.translated_text: nor on what is obtained by begging, nor on what remains after seizure, nor on a <s>Śrotriya</s>, nor on a renunciant, nor on a sacrifice. Thus.
A thief is not culpable [merely] from entering [a house].
But according to some, [he is culpable if] bearing weapons, [entering] by force, bearing wounds, or [clearly] identified [as a thief].
When a criminal is released [without punishment], the king should fast for one night.
The <s>purohita</s> (royal priest) [should fast] for three nights.
The <s>purohita</s> [should perform] a <s>kṛcchra</s> (penance) for punishing one who should not be punished.
The king [should fast] for three nights [in that case].
And they also cite [the following]:
In one who eats food [offered by a sinner], the sin of killing an embryo [resides]; in the husband, [the sin of] a wife's transgression;

body.text: Va.19.44 gurau śiṣyas^ca yājyas^ca stenas^rājani kilbiṣam (c)//
body.translated_text: in the teacher, [the sin of] the pupil; and in the officiant, [the sin of the one for whom he sacrifices]; in the king, [the sin of] a thief's transgression.

body.text: Va.19.45 rājabhis^dhṛta.daṇḍās tu kṛtvā(kṛ-) pāpāni mānavās^(c)/
body.translated_text: But men who have been punished by kings, having committed sins,
go to heaven, spotless, like virtuous men of good deeds.
Sin reaches the king who releases [a criminal] along with the transgression;

body.text: Va.19.46 tam^cet^vā ghātayet(han-)^rājā hanti(han-) dharmeṇa duṣkṛtam(c) iti //
body.translated_text: but if the king executes him, he destroys the evil deed through <s>dharma</s>. Thus.
For kings, in an emergency, purification is immediate;

body.text: Va.19.47 tathā na^ātyayike nityam^kālas^eva^atra kāraṇam(c) iti //
body.translated_text: but in non-emergency [situations], time alone is the cause [of purification] as always. Thus.
And here they cite a verse sung by <s>Yama</s>:

body.text: Va.19.48 na^adya doṣas^asti(as-) rājñām^vai vratinām^na ca satriṇām (c)/
body.translated_text: There is no fault today in kings, nor in those observing vows, nor in those performing <s>sattra</s> (long sacrificial sessions);

body.text: Va.19.48 aindra.sthānam upāsīnās(upa-ās-)^brahma.bhūtās^hi te sadā.(c) iti //
body.translated_text: for they, seated in the station of <s>Indra</s>, are always in a state of <s>Brahman</s>. Thus.
Are always in a state of <s>Brahman</s>—thus.
Penance [is prescribed] for an offense committed without deliberate intent.
According to some, even for one committed with deliberate intent.
The teacher is the discipliner of the self-controlled; the king is the discipliner of the wicked;
<s>Yama</s> <s>Vaivasvata</s> (son of the Sun) is the discipliner of those whose sins are hidden and uncaught. Thus.

body.text: Va.20.4 tatra ca sūrya.abhyuditas^san(as-)^ahas tiṣṭhet(sthā-) sāvitrīm^ca japet(jap-) //
body.translated_text: And there, standing facing the sun after sunrise, one should recite the <s>Sāvitrī</s> [mantra] throughout the day.
Likewise, [standing] facing the sun at sunset, one should sit [in meditation] at night.
One with discolored nails or dark teeth should perform a twelve-night <s>kṛcchra</s> (penance).

A <s>parivitti</s> (elder brother who remains unmarried while a younger marries), having performed a twelve-night <s>kṛcchra</s>, should marry—and he should marry that very [woman who was passed over].

body.text: Va.20.8 atha parivividānas^kṛcchra.atikṛcchrau caritvā(car-) tasmai dattvā(dā-) punar niviśeta(ni-viś-) tām^ca^eva^upayacchet(upa-yam-) //
body.translated_text: And a <s>parivividāna</s> (younger brother who marries before his elder), having performed both <s>kṛcchra</s> and <s>atikṛcchra</s> penances, and having given [a wife] to him [the elder brother], may marry again—and he should marry that very [woman].
The husband of a <s>agredidhiṣū</s> (a woman married before her elder sister), having performed a twelve-night <s>kṛcchra</s>, should marry—and he should marry her [properly].

body.text: Va.20.10 didhiṣū.patis^kṛcchra.atikṛcchrau caritvā(car-) tasmai dattvā(dā-) punar niviśet(ni-viś-) //
body.translated_text: The husband of a <s>didhiṣū</s> (a remarried woman), having performed both <s>kṛcchra</s> and <s>atikṛcchra</s>, and having given [a wife] to him [the first husband], may marry again.
The killing of a hero we shall explain later.
One who has abandoned the <s>Veda</s> (<s>brahma-ujjha</s>), having performed a twelve-night <s>kṛcchra</s>, should resume [the study of] the <s>Veda</s> from a teacher.

body.text: Va.20.13 guru.talpa.gas^sa.vṛṣaṇam^śiśnam uddhṛtya(ud-hṛ-)^añjalau^ādhāya(ā-dhā-) dakṣiṇā.mukhas^gacchet(gam-)^yatra^eva pratihanyāt(prati-han-) tatra tiṣṭhet(sthā-)^ā pralayam //
body.translated_text: One who violates the teacher's bed (<s>guru-talpa-ga</s>), having cut off his own penis with testicles and holding them in his cupped hands, should walk southward; wherever he falls, there he should remain until death.
Or, without [any] mark [of caste], smeared with ghee, he should embrace a heated iron pillar—he is purified by death, so it is known.
The same [applies] regarding [violation of] the wife of the teacher, the teacher's son, or the teacher's pupil.

body.text: Va.20.16 yoniṣu gurvīm^sakhīm^guru.sakhīm apapātram^patitām^ca gatvā(gam-) kṛcchra.abda.pādam^caret(car-) //
body.translated_text: Having gone to [i.e., had sexual relations with] a <s>gurvī</s> (teacher's wife), a female friend, a teacher's female friend, an outcaste, or a fallen woman, one should perform a quarter-year <s>kṛcchra</s>.

The same [penance applies] for eating food of a <s>Caṇḍāla</s> or a fallen person; thereafter, there is re-initiation (<s>punar-upanayana</s>), but the [rites of] shaving and so forth are not repeated.
And here they cite a verse from <s>Manu</s>:
Shaving, the girdle, the staff, begging for alms, and observances—

body.text: Va.20.18 etāni tu nivartante(ni-vṛt-) punar.saṃskāra.karmaṇi.(c) iti //
body.translated_text: these cease [i.e., are not repeated] in the rite of re-consecration (<s>punar-saṃskāra</s>). Thus.

body.text: Va.20.19 matyā madya.pāne tu^asurāyās^surāyās^ca^ajñāne kṛcchra.atikṛcchrau ghṛtam^prāśya(pra-aś-) punar.saṃskāras^ca //
body.translated_text: For unknowing drinking of <s>surā</s> (liquor) or <s>asurā</s> (fermented drink), [one should perform] both <s>kṛcchra</s> and <s>atikṛcchra</s>, drink ghee, and undergo re-consecration.
The same [applies] for consuming urine, excrement, or semen.

body.text: Va.20.21 madya.bhāṇḍe sthitās^āpas^yadi kas.cit^dvijas^pibet(pā-) padma.udumbara.bilva.palāśānām udakam^pītvā(pā-) tri.rātreṇa^eva śudhyati(śudh-) //
body.translated_text: If any twice-born person drinks water that has been stored in a liquor vessel, he is purified in three nights by drinking the decoction of lotus, <s>udumbara</s> (fig), <s>bilva</s> (wood-apple), and <s>palāśa</s> (flame tree).
But for habitual drinking of <s>surā</s>, a twice-born person should drink it fire-hot—he is purified by death, thus [it is declared].
We shall explain the [penance for] killing an embryo (<s>bhrūṇa-hatyā</s>): one who kills a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> becomes a killer of an embryo, as well as [one who destroys] an unidentified fetus.

body.text: Va.20.24 a.vijñātās^hi garbhās^pumāṃsas^bhavati(bhū-) tatmāt puṃs.kṛtyās^juhvati(hu-)^iti //{BṣPṣ tatmāt}{F tasmāt}
body.translated_text: For unidentified fetuses are [presumed to be] male; therefore they offer the <s>puṃsavana</s> (male-producing) rite, thus [it is declared].
The killer of an embryo, having set up the sacred fire, should offer these [oblations]:

body.text:
Va.20.26 lomāni mṛtyos^juhomi(hu-) lomabhis^mṛtyum^vāsaye(vas-)^iti prathamām^/ tvacam^mṛtyos^juhomi(hu-) tvacā mṛtyum^vāsaye(vas-)^iti dvitīyām^/ lohitam^mṛtyos^juhomi(hu-) lohitena mṛtyum^vāsaye(vas-)^iti tṛtīyām^/ māṃsam^mṛtyos^juhomi(hu-) māṃsena mṛtyum^vāsaye(vas-)^iti caturthīm^/ snāvāni mṛtyos^juhomi(hu-) snāvabhis^mṛtyum^vāsaye(vas-)^iti pañcamīm^/
medas^mṛtyos^juhomi(hu-) medasā ṛtyum^vāsaye(vas-)^iti ṣaṣṭhīm^/ asthīni mṛtyos^juhomi(hu-)^asthibhis^mṛtyum^vāsaye(vas-)^iti saptamīm^/ majjānam^mṛtyos^juhomi(hu-) majjābhis^mṛtyum^vāsaye(vas-)^iti^aṣṭamīm iti //
body.translated_text: 'I offer the hair to Death; with hair I clothe Death'—the first [oblation]; 'I offer the skin to Death; with skin I clothe Death'—the second; 'I offer the blood to Death; with blood I clothe Death'—the third; 'I offer the flesh to Death; with flesh I clothe Death'—the fourth; 'I offer the sinews to Death; with sinews I clothe Death'—the fifth; 'I offer the fat to Death; with fat I clothe Death'—the sixth; 'I offer the bones to Death; with bones I clothe Death'—the seventh; 'I offer the marrow to Death; with marrow I clothe Death'—the eighth.

body.text: Va.20.27 rāja.arthe brāhmaṇa.arthe vā saṃgrāme^abhimukham ātmānam^ghātayet(han-) //
body.translated_text: Or, for the sake of a king or a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, one should rush forward in battle and get oneself killed.
Or one who has been defeated three times [in battle against the person wronged] is purified—so it is known.
For it is declared that a sin that has been named [i.e., confessed] becomes less.
And they also cite [the following]:
Having called a fallen person 'fallen,' or again, a thief 'thief,'
by [false] speech one incurs equal guilt; [and] by falsehood, one incurs double guilt. Thus.
Likewise, for killing a <s>Kṣatriya</s> (member of the warrior class), one should perform [penance] for eight years.
Six [years] for [killing] a <s>Vaiśya</s>.
Three [years] for [killing] a <s>Śūdra</s>.
And for killing a <s>Brāhmaṇī</s> (Brahmin woman) who is an <s>Ātreyī</s>, and for [killing] a <s>Kṣatriya</s> or <s>Vaiśya</s> during the <s>Savana</s> (Soma pressing).
We shall explain <s>Ātreyī</s>: they call <s>Ātreyī</s> a woman who has had her menstrual period and has bathed after it [i.e., is in her fertile period].
For in her, future offspring exists.
For [killing] a non-<s>Ātreyī</s> [woman], the penance for killing a <s>Kṣatriya</s> [applies].
For [killing] a <s>Kṣatriya</s> [woman], the penance for killing a <s>Vaiśya</s> [applies].
For [killing] a <s>Vaiśya</s> [woman], the penance for killing a <s>Śūdra</s> [applies].
For killing a <s>Śūdra</s> [woman], one year [of penance].

body.text: Va.20.41 brāhmaṇa.suvarṇa.haraṇe prakīrya(pra-kṝ-) keśān rājānam abhidhāvet(abhi-dhāv-) stenas^asmi(as-) bho śāstu(śās-) mām^bhavān iti tasmai rājā^audumbaram^śastram^dadyāt(dā-) tena^ātmānam^pramāpayet(pra-mā-)^maraṇāt pūtas^bhavati(bhū-)^iti vijñāyate(vi-jñā-) //{BṣPṣ bho}{F bhos.}
body.translated_text: For stealing the gold of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, letting his hair loose, one should run to the king [saying]: 'I am a thief, Sir! Let your honor punish me.' The king should give him a club of <s>udumbara</s> wood; with that he should kill himself—he is purified by death, so it is known.

body.text: Va.20.42 niṣkālakas^vā ghṛta.aktas^gomaya.agninā pāda.prabhṛti^ātmānam abhidāhayet(abhi-dah-)^maraṇāt pūtas^bhavati(bhū-)^iti vijñāyate(vi-jñā-) //
body.translated_text: Or, without [any caste] mark, smeared with ghee, one should burn oneself with a fire of cow dung, from the feet upward—he is purified by death, so it is known.
And they also cite [the following]:
Those who die before their time, [having committed] various sinful deeds,
when they obtain bodies again, hear [what becomes] their limbs:

body.text: Va.20.44 stenas^ku.nakhī bhavati(bhū-) śvitrī bhavati(bhū-) brahma.hā (c)/
body.translated_text: A thief becomes one with deformed nails; a killer of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> becomes a leper;

body.text: Va.20.44 surā.pas^śyāva.dantas tu duścarmā guru.talpa.gas.(c) iti //
body.translated_text: a drinker of <s>surā</s> becomes one with dark teeth; and one who violates the teacher's bed becomes one with diseased skin. Thus.

body.text: Va.20.45 patita.saṃprayoge ca brāhmeṇa vā yaunena vā yās tebhyas^sakāśāt^mātrās^upalabdhās tāsām^parityāgas tais^ca na saṃvaset(sam-vas-) //
body.translated_text: And in the case of association with fallen persons, whether through <s>Brāhma</s> (priestly) or <s>Yauna</s> (marital) [connection]—whatever materials (<s>mātrā</s>) have been received from them, those should be abandoned, and one should not live with them.
(20.46) Having gone to the northern direction, not eating, studying the <s>Saṃhitā</s>, one becomes purified—thus it is known.
(20.47) And they also cite [the following]:
(20.47) By bodily mortification, by austerity, and by study,
(20.47) the evil-doer is freed from sin; and by giving also one is released.
(20.47) Thus it is known, it is known.

body.text: Va.21.1 śūdras^cet^brāhmaṇīm abhigacchet(abhi-gam-)^vīraṇais^veṣṭayitvā(veṣṭ-) śūdram agnau prāsyet(pra-as-)^brāhmaṇyās^śirasi vapanam^kārayitvā(kṛ-) sarpiṣā samabhyajya(sam-abhi-añj-) nagnām^kṛṣṇa.kharam āropya(ā-ruh-) mahā.patham anusaṃvrājayet(anu-sam-vraj-) pūtā bhavati(bhū-)^iti vijñāyate(vi-jñā-) //
body.translated_text: (21.1) If a <s>Śūdra</s> approaches a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> woman, having wrapped the <s>Śūdra</s> with <s>vīraṇa</s> grass, one should cast him into the fire; having had the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> woman's head shaved and having anointed her with ghee, one should mount her naked upon a black donkey and make her walk along the main road. She becomes purified—thus it is known.

body.text: Va.21.2 vaiśyas^cet^brāhmaṇīm abhigacchet(abhi-gam-)^lohita.darbhais^veṣṭayitvā(veṣṭ-) vaiśyam agnau prāsyet(pra-as-)^brāhmaṇyās^śirasi vapanam^kārayitvā(kṛ-) sarpiṣā samabhyajya(sam-abhi-añj-) nagnām^gaura.kharam āropya(ā-ruh-) mahā.patham anusaṃvrājayet(anu-sam-vraj-) pūtā bhavati(bhū-)^iti vijñāyate(vi-jñā-) //
body.translated_text: (21.2) If a <s>Vaiśya</s> approaches a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> woman, having wrapped the <s>Vaiśya</s> with red <s>darbha</s> grass, one should cast him into the fire; having had the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> woman's head shaved and having anointed her with ghee, one should mount her naked upon a tawny donkey and make her walk along the main road. She becomes purified—thus it is known.

body.text: Va.21.3 rājanyas^cet^brāhmaṇīm abhigacchet(abhi-gam-)^śara.patrais^veṣṭayitvā(veṣṭ-) rājanyam agnau prāsyet(pra-as)^brāhmaṇyās^śirasi vapanam^kārayitvā(kṛ-) sarpiṣā samabhyajya(sam-abhi-añj-) nagnām^śveta.kharam āropya(ā-ruh-) mahā.patham anusaṃvrājayet(anu-sam-vraj-) pūtā bhavati(bhū-)^iti vijñāyate(vi-jñā-) //
body.translated_text: (21.3) If a <s>Rājanya</s> approaches a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> woman, having wrapped the <s>Rājanya</s> with arrow-leaf coverings, one should cast him into the fire; having had the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> woman's head shaved and having anointed her with ghee, one should mount her naked upon a white donkey and make her walk along the main road. She becomes purified—thus it is known.
(21.4) Similarly [the rule applies for] a <s>Vaiśya</s> [who approaches] a <s>Rājanya</s> woman.
(21.5) And a <s>Śūdra</s> [who approaches] a <s>Rājanya</s> or <s>Vaiśya</s> woman.

body.text: Va.21.6 manasā bhartus^aticāre tri.rātram^yāvakam^kṣīrodanam^vā bhuñjānā(bhuj-)^adhas^śayīta(śī-)^ūrdhvam^tri.rātrāt^apsu nimagnāyās^sāvitryā^aṣṭa.śatena śirobhis^juhuyāt(hu-) pūtā bhavati(bhū-)^iti vijñāyate(vi-jñā-) //{BṣPṣ kṣīrodanam}{F kṣīra.odanam}
body.translated_text: (21.6) [If a woman] has transgressed against her husband in thought, she should eat barley gruel or milk-rice for three nights and sleep on the ground; after the three nights, having immersed herself in water, she should offer oblations with eight hundred [repetitions of] the <s>Sāvitrī</s> [while water is poured] over her head. She becomes purified—thus it is known.

body.text: Va.21.7 vāc.saṃbandhe^etat^eva māsam^caritvā(car-)^ūrdhvam^māsāt^apsu nimagnāyās^sāvitryās^caturbhis^aṣṭa.śatais^śirobhis^juhuyāt(hu-) pūtā bhavati(bhū-)^iti vijñāyate(vi-jñā-) //
body.translated_text: (21.7) In the case of transgression by speech, having performed this same [penance] for a month, after the month, having immersed herself in water, she should offer with four times eight hundred [repetitions of] the <s>Sāvitrī</s> [poured] over her head. She becomes purified—thus it is known.

body.text: Va.21.8 vyavāye tu saṃvatsaram^ghṛta.paṭam^dhārayet(dhṛ-)^go.maya.garte kuśa.prastare vā śayīta(śī-)^ūrdhvam^saṃvatsarāt^apsu nimagnāyās^sāvitrī.aṣṭa.śatena śirobhis^juhuyāt(hu-) pūtā bhavati(bhū-)^iti vijñāyate(vi-jñā-) //
body.translated_text: (21.8) But in the case of sexual intercourse, she should wear a garment smeared with ghee for a year and sleep in a cow-dung pit or on a bed of <s>kuśa</s> grass; after the year, having immersed herself in water, she should offer with eight hundred [repetitions of] the <s>Sāvitrī</s> [poured] over her head. She becomes purified—thus it is known.

body.text: Va.21.9 vyavāye tīrtha.gamane dharmebhyas tu nivartate(ni-vṛt-) (c)//
body.translated_text: (21.9) In the case of sexual intercourse, by going on a pilgrimage (<s>tīrtha</s>), she turns away from [further] righteous acts.

body.text: Va.21.10 catasras tu parityājyās(pari-tyaj-)^śiṣya.gā guru.gā ca yā (c)/
body.translated_text: (21.10) But four [kinds of women] are to be abandoned: one who goes to a pupil, one who goes to a teacher,

body.text: Va.21.10 pati.ghnī ca viśeṣeṇa juṅgita.upagatā ca yā (c)//
body.translated_text: (21.10) a husband-slayer especially, and one who has approached a man of mixed caste.

body.text: Va.21.11 yā brāhmaṇī ca surā.pī na tām^devās^patilokam^nayanti(nī-)^iha^eva sā carati(car-) kṣīṇa.puṇyā^apsu luk^bhavati(bhū-) śuktikā vā //
body.translated_text: (21.11) A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> woman who drinks liquor—the gods do not lead her to her husband's world; she wanders here with exhausted merit and becomes in water a leech or an oyster shell.
(21.12) Women of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>Kṣatriya</s>, and <s>Vaiśya</s> [classes] who have had intercourse with a <s>Śūdra</s>—
(21.12) those without offspring are purified by expiation (<s>prāyaścitta</s>); not the others.
(21.13) Those who have acted in inverse [caste] order should perform the <s>Kṛcchra</s> followed by the <s>Cāndrāyaṇa</s>.
(21.14) For devoted wives, housewives, women of truth-vows, and women of purity-vows—
(21.14) their worlds are equal to those of their husbands; but for adulterous women, the worlds of jackals.
(21.15) Half the body falls of him whose wife drinks liquor;
(21.15) for one whose half-body has fallen, no expiation is prescribed.

(21.16) If a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> approaches another <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>'s wife without premeditation—for one who has not ceased his religious duties, [the penance is] <s>Kṛcchra</s>; for one who has ceased his religious duties, <s>Atikṛcchra</s>.
(21.17) Similarly for [the wife of] a <s>Rājanya</s> or <s>Vaiśya</s>.
(21.18) If one kills a cow, wrapped in the fresh hide of that [cow], he should perform the <s>Kṛcchra</s> for six months or the <s>Tapta-Kṛcchra</s>.
(21.19) The procedure for these two [is as follows]:

body.text: Va.21.20 tri.aham^divā bhuṅke(bhuj-) naktam aśnāti(aś-) vai tri.aham api (c)/
body.translated_text: (21.20) For three days one eats during the day; for three days one eats at night;

body.text: Va.21.20 tri.aham ayācita.vratas tri.aham^na bhuj^iti kṛcchras^(c)//
body.translated_text: (21.20) for three days one observes the vow of [eating] unbegged [food]; and for three days one does not eat—this is the <s>Kṛcchra</s>.
(21.21) For three days one should drink hot water; for three days one should drink hot milk;
(21.21) for three days, having drunk hot ghee, one should live on air for the remaining three days—
(21.21) this is the <s>Tapta-Kṛcchra</s>.
(21.22) And one should give a bull and a draft-animal.
(21.23) And they also cite [the following]:
(21.23) Formerly there were only three diseases: envy, not eating, and old age;
(21.23) by killing spotted deer, goats, and birds, [man] brought about ninety-eight [more diseases].
(21.24) Having killed a dog, cat, mongoose, snake, frog, or mouse, one should perform the twelve-night <s>Kṛcchra</s> and give something [as a gift].
(21.25) Having killed a heap the size of a cow of boneless creatures, one should perform the twelve-night <s>Kṛcchra</s> and give something [as a gift].
(21.26) But for creatures with bones, [the penance applies] for each one individually.

body.text: Va.21.27 yas^agnīn apavidhyet(apa-vyadh-) kṛcchram^dvādaśa.rātram^caritvā(car-) punar ādhānam^kārayet(kṛ-) //
body.translated_text: (21.27) One who extinguishes the sacred fires, having performed the twelve-night <s>Kṛcchra</s>, should have the [fires] established again.
(21.28) In the case of a guru's false accusation, having bathed with one's garments on, one should appease the guru. By his being appeased, one becomes purified—thus it is known.
(21.29) An atheist (<s>nāstika</s>), having performed the twelve-night <s>Kṛcchra</s>, should desist from atheism.
(21.30) But for one who [continues to] lead the life of an atheist, [the penance is] <s>Atikṛcchra</s>.
(21.31) By this, [the case of] the seller of <s>Soma</s> is [also] explained.
(21.32) A forest-dweller (<s>vānaprastha</s>), upon breaking his consecration, having performed the twelve-night <s>Kṛcchra</s>, should kindle [the fire] anew in a great forest thicket.

(21.33) For mendicants (<s>bhikṣus</s>), [the procedure is] like that of a forest-dweller: the <s>Soma</s>-augmentation ceremony, and the sacraments of their own respective texts—and the sacraments of their own respective texts.

body.text: Va.22.1 atha khalu^ayam^puruṣas^mithyā vyākaroti(vi-ā-kṛ-)^a.yājyam^vā yājayati(yaj-)^a.pratigrāhyam^vā pratigṛhṇāti(prati-grah-)^an.annam^vā^aśnāti(aś-)^an.ācaraṇīyam(ā-car-) eva^ācarati(ā-car-) //
body.translated_text: (22.1) Now, when a person speaks falsely, or officiates for an unworthy person, or accepts what should not be accepted, or eats food that should not be eaten, or performs what should not be performed—
(22.2) regarding that, they deliberate: 'Should one perform expiation (<s>prāyaścitta</s>), or should one not?'
(22.3) 'One should not'—they say.
(22.4) For <s>karma</s> is not diminished [by expiation].
(22.5) 'One should indeed [perform expiation]'—because of the Vedic evidence for that.

body.text: Va.22.6 tarati(tṛ-) sarvam^pāpmānam^tarati(tṛ-) brahma.hattyām^yas^aśvamedhena yajate(yaj-)^iti //{BṣPṣ hattyām.}{F hatyām.}
body.translated_text: (22.6) 'One crosses over all sin, one crosses over the sin of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>-slaying, who sacrifices with the <s>Aśvamedha</s>'—[thus the <s>Veda</s> says].
(22.7) And thus, one who is accused should sacrifice with the <s>Gosava</s> or the <s>Agniṣṭut</s>.
(22.8) The means of redemption for that [sin] are: recitation (<s>japa</s>), austerity (<s>tapas</s>), oblation (<s>homa</s>), fasting (<s>upavāsa</s>), and giving (<s>dāna</s>).

body.text: Va.22.9 upaniṣadas^veda.ādayas^veda.antās^sarva.chandas.sāṃhitās^madhūni^aghamarṣaṇam atharvaśiras^rudrās^puruṣasūktam^rājana(cf^rājaṇa).rauhiṇe sāmanī kūṣmāṇḍāni pāvamānyas^sāvitrī ca^iti pāvanāni //
body.translated_text: (22.9) The <s>Upaniṣads</s>, the beginnings of the <s>Vedas</s>, the ends of the <s>Vedas</s>, all collections of Vedic meters, the <s>Madhus</s> (honey-texts), the <s>Aghamarṣaṇa</s>, the <s>Atharvaśiras</s>, the <s>Rudras</s>, the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s>, the <s>Rājana</s> and <s>Rauhiṇa</s> <s>Sāmans</s>, the <s>Kūṣmāṇḍas</s>, the <s>Pāvamānīs</s>, and the <s>Sāvitrī</s>—these are the purifying [texts].
(22.10) And they also cite [the following]:
(22.10) The <s>Vaiśvānarī</s>, the <s>Vrātapatī</s>, and the <s>Pavitreṣṭi</s> as well—
(22.10) one who employs [these] once during the season purifies [up to] ten generations.

body.text: Va.22.11 upavāsa.nyāyena payas.vratatā phala.bhakṣatā prasṛta.yāvakas^hiraṇya.prāśanam^soma.pānam iti medhyāni //
body.translated_text: (22.11) By the method of fasting: milk-diet (<s>payovrata</s>), fruit-diet (<s>phalabhakṣa</s>), [a specific measure of] barley-gruel (<s>prasṛta-yāvaka</s>), drinking gold-[water] (<s>hiraṇya-prāśana</s>), and <s>Soma</s>-drinking—these are the purifying [substances].
(22.12) All heaps of stones, all flowing streams, holy lakes, pilgrimage sites (<s>tīrthas</s>), hermitages of sages, and cow-pens—these are the [purifying] places.
(22.13) A year, a month, twenty-four days, twelve days, six days, three days, and a day-and-night—these are the [purifying] time periods.
(22.14) In the absence of a specific prescription, these may be employed alternatively.

body.text: Va.22.15 enaḥsu guruṣu gurūṇi laghuṣu laghūni //
body.translated_text: (22.15) For grave offenses, heavy [penances]; for light [offenses], light [penances].
(22.16) The <s>Kṛcchra</s>, the <s>Atikṛcchra</s>, and the <s>Cāndrāyaṇa</s>—these are the universal expiations. The universal expiations.

body.text: Va.23.1 brahmacārī cet striyam upeyāt(upa-i-)^araṇye catuṣpathe laukike^agnau rakṣas.daivatam^gardabham^paśum ālabhet(ā-labh-) //
body.translated_text: (23.1) If a celibate student (<s>brahmacārin</s>) approaches a woman, at a crossroads in the wilderness, he should sacrifice a donkey as an offering to the <s>Rakṣas</s>-deity in a secular fire.
(23.2) Or he should offer a <s>Nairṛta</s> cake-offering (<s>caru</s>).

body.text: Va.23.3 tasya juhuyāt(hu-) kāmāya svāhā kāma.kāmāya svāhā nairṛtyai svāhā rakṣas.devatābhyas^svāhā^iti //
body.translated_text: (23.3) Into that [fire] he should make oblations [saying]: 'To <s>Kāma</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Kāma-kāma</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Nairṛtī</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To the <s>Rakṣas</s>-deities, <s>svāhā</s>!'

body.text: Va.23.4 etat^eva retasas^prayatna.utsarge divā svapne vrata.antareṣu vā samāvartanāt //
body.translated_text: (23.4) This same [penance applies] for deliberate emission of semen—whether during the day, in a dream, or during other observances—until the completion [of studentship].
(23.5) For intercourse with an animal, one should give a white bull.
(23.6) The offense of approaching a cow is explained by [the rule for] the killing of a <s>Śūdra</s> woman.
(23.7) For a celibate student (<s>brahmacārin</s>), there is cessation of the vow [only] for funeral rites.
(23.8) Except for [the funeral rites of] mother and father.
(23.9) If he [the student] should fall ill, he may eat any leftover food of the guru for the purpose of medicine—thus it is known.

body.text: Va.23.10 guruprayuktas^cet^mriyeta(mṛ-) trīn kṛcchān^caret(car-)^gurus^//{BṣPṣ kṛcchān}{F kṛcchrān}
body.translated_text: (23.10) If [a student] dies while engaged [in a task] by the guru, the guru should perform three <s>Kṛcchras</s>.
(23.11) If a celibate student (<s>brahmacārin</s>) eats meat, having performed the twelve-night <s>Kṛcchra</s> [prescribed for] eating leftover food, he should complete the remainder of his vow.
(23.12) And the same [applies] for eating at <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestor) meals and birth-impurity (<s>sūtaka</s>) meals.

body.text: Va.23.13 a.kāmata.upanatam^madhu vājasaneyake na duṣyati(duṣ-)^iti vijñāyate(vi-jñā-) //
body.translated_text: (23.13) Honey that comes [to a student] without his seeking is not a fault, according to the <s>Vājasaneyaka</s>—thus it is known.
(23.14) One who commits suicide and is [thereby] accused—for his <s>sapiṇḍa</s> relatives, there is cessation of the funeral rites.
(23.15) One who kills himself by means of wood, water, clod, stone, weapon, poison, or rope—he is a self-slayer (<s>ātmahā</s>).
(23.16) And they also cite [the following]:
(23.16) A twice-born (<s>dvija</s>) who, out of affection, performs funeral rites for a suicide—
(23.16) he should observe the <s>Cāndrāyaṇa</s> vow combined with the <s>Tapta-Kṛcchra</s>.
(23.17) We shall explain the <s>Cāndrāyaṇa</s> later.
(23.18) For [mere] resolve to kill oneself, [the penance is] three nights.

body.text: Va.23.19 jīvan(jīv-)^ātmatyāgī kṛchraṃ dvādaśa.rātram^caret(car-) tri.rātram^hi^upavaset(upa-vas-)^nityam^snigdhena vāsasā prāṇān ātmani ca^āyamya(ā-yam-) tris^paṭhet(paṭh-)^aghamarṣaṇam iti //{BṣPṣ kṛchraṃ}{F kṛcchraṃ}
body.translated_text: (23.19) A surviving suicide-attempter should perform the twelve-night <s>Kṛcchra</s>; and he should fast for three nights, always wearing wet garments, restraining the breaths within himself, he should recite the <s>Aghamarṣaṇa</s> three times—thus it is known.
(23.20) Or by this method, one should repeat the <s>Gāyatrī</s> [in the same manner].
Or, having set up the fire, one should offer ghee with the <s>Kūṣmāṇḍa</s> [mantras].
And whatever [sin] is other than the great sins — all of it is purified by this [rite]. Thus.

body.text: Va.23.23 atha^api^ācamet(ā-cam-)^agnis^ca mā manyus(man-)^ca^iti prātarmanasā pāpam^dhyātvoṃpūrvās^satyāntā vyāhṛtīs^japet(jap-)^aghamarṣaṇam^vā paṭhet(paṭh-) //{dhyātvoṃpūrvās < dhyātvā(dhyā-). oṃpūrvās}
body.translated_text: Moreover, one should sip water [reciting] 'May <s>Agni</s> and <s>Manyu</s> [protect me]'; having meditated on the sin in the morning, one should recite the <s>vyāhṛtis</s> beginning with <s>Oṃ</s> and ending with <s>Satya</s>, or recite the <s>Aghamarṣaṇa</s> [hymn].
Having touched a moist human bone, [there is] impurity for three days.
But for a dry [bone], [impurity lasts] one day and one night.
And the same [applies] for following a corpse.
When an [uninvited] arrival comes among those who are studying, [there should be] no eating for one day and night.
For three nights, [there should be] purificatory bathing, and mutual avoidance.
For [touching] dogs, cats, mongooses, or swift-moving [creatures], [impurity lasts] one day and night.

For eating the flesh of a dog, rooster, domestic pig, heron, vulture, <s>bhāsa</s> (a bird of prey), pigeon, human, crow, or owl — fasting for seven nights, [continuing] until the bowels are emptied, consuming ghee, and re-consecration.

body.text: Va.23.31 brāhmaṇas tu śunā daṣṭas^nadīm^gatvā(gam-) samudra.gām (c)/
body.translated_text: But a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who has been bitten by a dog, having gone to a river flowing to the sea,
Having performed a hundred <s>prāṇāyāmas</s> and consumed ghee, is thereby purified. Thus.
Upon touching a dog, a <s>Caṇḍāla</s>, or a fallen person, one becomes purified immediately by bathing with one's garments on — so it is known.
Upon hearing the cry of a fallen person or a <s>Caṇḍāla</s>, for three nights they should remain with speech restrained and without eating.
Or, by repeating [the sacred texts] up to a thousand [times], they become purified — so it is known.

By this same [procedure], those who teach or officiate at sacrifice for condemned persons are explained [to be purified]; and by abandoning the fee (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>), they become purified — so it is known.
By this same [procedure], one who has been [falsely] accused is explained [to be purified].

body.text: Va.23.38 bhrūṇa.hattyāyām^dvādaśa.rātram ab.bhakṣas^dvādaśa.rātram upavaset(upa-vas-) //{BṣPṣ hattyāyām.}{F hatyāyām.}
body.translated_text: In the case of embryo-killing (<s>bhrūṇahatyā</s>), [one should subsist] for twelve days on water alone and fast for twelve days.

body.text: Va.23.39 brāhmaṇam anṛtena^abhiśaṃsya(abhi-śaṃs-) patanīyena^upapatanīyena vā māsam ab.bhakṣas^śuddhavatīs^āvartayet(ā-vṛt-) //
body.translated_text: Having falsely accused a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> of a mortal sin (<s>patanīya</s>) or a secondary sin (<s>upapatanīya</s>), [one should subsist] on water alone for a month and recite the <s>Śuddhavatī</s> [verses].
Or one may go to the purificatory bath (<s>avabhṛtha</s>) of a horse sacrifice (<s>aśvamedha</s>).
By this same [procedure], sexual intercourse with a <s>Caṇḍāla</s> woman is explained [to be expiated].
Now, another rule for <s>kṛcchra</s> (penance), which is general and widely applied:

body.text: Va.23.43 ahar^prātar ahar naktamahar ekam ayācitam (c)/
body.translated_text: A day [eating only] in the morning, a day [only] at night, a day [only eating] what is obtained unsolicited,
A day of complete abstinence — [this is] one cycle; thus [are] the two periods of four days.
For the benefit of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Manu</s>, the foremost upholder of <s>dharma</s>,
Proclaimed this <s>śiśukṛcchra</s> (child-penance) [applicable] to children, the elderly, and the sick.
Now [follows] the rule of the <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s> (lunar penance).
At the beginning of the dark fortnight of the month, one should eat fourteen morsels;
One should eat with increasing [numbers of] morsels and complete the rest of the fortnight.

body.text: Va.23.45 evam^hi śukla.pakṣa.ādau grāsam ekam^tu bhakṣayet(bhakṣ-) (c)/
body.translated_text: Similarly, at the beginning of the bright fortnight, one should eat only one morsel;
One should eat with decreasing [numbers of] morsels and complete the rest of the fortnight.

body.text: Va.23.46 atra^eva gāyet(gai-) sāmāni api vā vyāhṛtīs^japet(jap-) (c)//
body.translated_text: During this [penance], one should sing <s>Sāman</s> [chants] or recite the <s>vyāhṛtis</s>.
This <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s> month, purifying and praised by sages,
Is prescribed as expiation (<s>prāyaścitta</s>) for all [sins that are] unspecified.
Is prescribed. Thus.
Now [follows] the <s>atikṛcchra</s> (super-penance).

body.text: Va.24.2 tri.aham^prātar^tathā sāyam ayācitam^parākas^iti kṛcchras^yāvat sakṛt^ādadīta(ā-dā-) tāvat^aśnīyāt(aś-) pūrvavat sas^atikṛcchras^//
body.translated_text: Three days [eating only] in the morning, likewise three days [only] in the evening, three days [only what is] unsolicited, and three days of total abstinence — this is the <s>kṛcchra</s>. But one should eat [only] as much as one can take up in a single [handful]; as before — that is the <s>atikṛcchra</s>.
A <s>kṛcchra</s> [performed] on water alone — that is the <s>kṛcchrātikṛcchra</s> (penance-super-penance).
The observances of the penances [are as follows]:

body.text: Va.24.5 śmaśru.keśān vāpayet(vap-)^bhruvas.akṣi.loma.śikhā.varjam^nakhān nikṛtya(ni-kṛt-)^eka.vāsas^anindita.bhojī [sakṛt^bhaikṣam aninditaṃ] triṣavaṇam udaka.upasparśī daṇḍī kamaṇḍalus^strī.śūdra.saṃbhāṣaṇa.varjī sthāna.āsana.śīlas^ahar^tiṣṭhet(sthā-)^rātrau^asīta(as-)^iti^āha bhagavān vasiṣṭhas^//
body.translated_text: One should shave the beard and hair, except the eyebrows, eyelashes, and topknot (<s>śikhā</s>); cut the nails; wear a single garment; eat blameless [food] — [eating] blameless alms-food once [a day]; bathe three times [a day]; carry a staff and water-pot (<s>kamaṇḍalu</s>); avoid conversation with women and <s>Śūdras</s>; be given to standing and sitting [in meditation]; stand during the day and sit at night — thus says the venerable <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>.

body.text: Va.24.6 sa tat^yat^etat^dharma.śāstram^na^a.putrāya na^a.śiṣyāya na^a.saṃvatsara.uṣitāya dadyāt(dā-) //
body.translated_text: This <s>dharmaśāstra</s> should not be given to one without a son, nor to one without a disciple, nor to one who has not resided [with the teacher] for a year.
The fee (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>) is a thousand [cows] together with eleven bulls, or [it may be given by] the grace of the teacher, or by the grace of the teacher. Thus.
I shall now describe without remainder the purification for great sins whose faults have not been publicly disclosed,
And for all secondary sins.
For one who has established the sacred fires, who is disciplined, aged, or learned —
The expiation (<s>prāyaścitta</s>) is to be performed in secret; for all others, the previously stated [public penance applies].
