Through <s>prāṇāyāmas</s>, purifications, gifts, fire-offerings, and recitations,
Those who are constantly devoted are freed from sins; there is no doubt.
<s>Prāṇāyāmas</s>, purificatory [mantras], <s>vyāhṛtis</s>, and <s>praṇava</s> (Oṃ) —
Seated with purified hands, one should practice the daily <s>Brahman</s> (Vedic recitation).
Ever devoted, repeatedly performing <s>prāṇāyāmas</s>,

body.text: Va.25.5 ā loma.agrāt^nakha.agrāt^ca tapas tapyatu(tap-) uttamam (c)//
body.translated_text: From the tips of the hairs to the tips of the nails, one should practice the supreme austerity.
From restraint [of breath], wind arises; from wind, fire is produced;
From heat, waters arise; then the inner self is purified by [these] three.

body.text: Va.25.7 na tām^tīvreṇa tapasā na svādhyāyais^na ca^ijyayā (c)/
body.translated_text: That goal which, through intense austerity, nor through self-study, nor through sacrifice,

body.text: Va.25.7 gatim^gantum^dvijās^śaktās^yogāt saṃprā vanti yām (c)//{BṣPṣ saṃprā vanti}{F saṃprāpnuvanti(sam-pra-āp-)}
body.translated_text: The twice-born are unable to reach — that they attain through <s>yoga</s>.
Through <s>yoga</s>, knowledge is attained; <s>yoga</s> is the mark of <s>dharma</s>;
<s>Yoga</s> is the supreme eternal austerity; therefore, one should always be devoted [to it].

body.text: Va.25.9 praṇave nitya.yuktas syāt(as-)^vyāhṛtīṣu ca saptasu (c)/
body.translated_text: One should be constantly devoted to <s>praṇava</s> (Oṃ), to the seven <s>vyāhṛtis</s>,
And to the three-footed <s>Gāyatrī</s> — [then] no fear exists anywhere.
From <s>praṇava</s> the <s>Vedas</s> [emerge], and in <s>praṇava</s> they are established;
<s>Praṇava</s> is all that is made of speech; therefore, one should practice <s>praṇava</s>.
The single syllable [Oṃ] is the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, remembered as the highest purifier.
When a commingling of all sins has occurred,
Ten thousand repetitions of the <s>Sāvitrī</s> is the great purification.
One should recite the <s>Gāyatrī</s> with the <s>vyāhṛtis</s>, with <s>praṇava</s>, and with the <s>śiras</s> (head verse),
Three times, with extended breath — that is called <s>prāṇāyāma</s>.
That is called [<s>prāṇāyāma</s>]. Thus.

body.text: Va.26.1 prāṇāyāmān dhārayet(dhṛ-) ttrīnyas^yathāvidhi^atandritas^(c)/{BṣPṣ ttrīn}{F trīn}
body.translated_text: One who diligently holds three <s>prāṇāyāmas</s> according to rule —
The sin committed during the day and night is destroyed that very instant.

body.text: Va.26.2 karmaṇā manasā vācā yat^ahnā kṛtam ainasam (c)/
body.translated_text: Whatever sin has been committed during the day by action, mind, or speech —
Seated at the evening <s>sandhyā</s> (twilight worship), one removes it through <s>prāṇāyāmas</s>.

body.text: Va.26.3 karmaṇā manasā vācā yat^rātryā kṛtam ainasam (c)/
body.translated_text: Whatever sin has been committed during the night by action, mind, or speech —
Rising at the morning <s>sandhyā</s>, one removes it through <s>prāṇāyāmas</s>.
Sixteen <s>prāṇāyāmas</s> with <s>vyāhṛtis</s> and <s>praṇava</s>,
Performed daily, purify even the killer of an embryo within a month.

body.text: Va.26.5 japtvā(jap-) kautsam apa^iti^etadvāsiṣṭham^ca tricam^prati (c)/(cf^ṛV.<1.097.01a> apa naḥ śośucad agham agne śuśugdhy ā rayim |ṛV.<7.080.01a> prati stomebhir uṣasaṃ vasiṣṭhā gīrbhir viprāsaḥ prathamā abudhran |)
body.translated_text: Having recited the <s>Kautsa</s> [hymn], the 'Apa' (Away) [hymn], the <s>Vāsiṣṭha</s> triplet,
The <s>Māhitra</s> [hymn], and the <s>Śuddhavatī</s> [verses] — even a drinker of <s>surā</s> (liquor) is purified.
Having recited even once the <s>Asyavāmīya</s> [hymn] and the <s>Śivasaṅkalpa</s> [hymn] —
Even one who has stolen gold becomes free from stain in an instant.

body.text: Va.26.7 haviṣyantīyam abhyasya(abhi-as-) na tam aṃhas^iti tricam^(c)/(cf^ṛV.<10.126.01ab> na tam aṃho na duritaṃ devāso aṣṭa martyam |)
body.translated_text: Having studied the <s>Haviṣyantīya</s> [hymn] and the triplet beginning with 'na tam aṃhas' (no evil [touches] him),
And having recited the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s> — one who has violated the teacher's bed is freed.

body.text:
Va.26.8 api vā^apsu nimajjānas tris^japet(jap-)^aghamarṣaṇam (c)/
Va.26.8 yathā^aśvamedha.avabhṛthas tādṛśam^manus^abravīt(brū-) (c)//
body.translated_text: Or, plunging into water, one should recite the <s>Aghamarṣaṇa</s> [hymn] three times — <s>Manu</s> declared that [its effect] is like the purificatory bath (<s>avabhṛtha</s>) of the horse sacrifice (<s>aśvamedha</s>).
Compared to the performed sacrifice (<s>ārambhayajña</s>), the sacrifice of recitation (<s>japayajña</s>) is ten times superior;
The whispered [recitation] (<s>upāṃśu</s>) is a hundredfold [superior]; the mental [recitation] (<s>mānasa</s>) is remembered as a thousandfold [superior].
The four <s>pākayajñas</s> (cooked-food sacrifices), together with the ritual sacrifices —

body.text: Va.26.10 sarve te japa.yajñasya kalām^na^arhanti(arh-) ṣoḍaśīm (c)//
body.translated_text: All of them are not worth a sixteenth part of the sacrifice of recitation.
By recitation alone, indeed, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> attains perfection — there is no doubt about this;
Whether he performs other [rites] or not, he who is friendly is called a [true] <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.
Those who recite, who offer oblations, who meditate, who dwell at holy places (<s>tīrtha</s>),

body.text: Va.26.12 na parivasanti(pari-vas-) pāpāni ye ca snātās^śiras.vratais^(c)//
body.translated_text: And who have bathed with head-vows (<s>śirovrata</s>) — sins do not cling to them.
Just as fire, fanned by wind, blazes up with oblations,
So a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> ever devoted to recitation blazes forth.

body.text:
Va.26.14 sva.adhyāya.adhyāyinām^nityam^nityam^ca prayata.ātmanām (c)/
Va.26.14 japatām(jap-)^juhvatām(hu-)^ca^api vinipātas^na vidyate(vid-) (c)//
body.translated_text: For those who constantly study the <s>Veda</s> through self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>), who are ever self-controlled, who recite and offer oblations — there is no downfall.
The divine [<s>Gāyatrī</s>], with a thousand [repetitions] as the highest, a hundred as the middle, and ten as the least —
One desiring purification should employ [it], even when established in all sins.
A <s>Kṣatriya</s> should overcome his calamity through the strength of his arms;

body.text: Va.26.16 dhanena vaiśya.śudrau tu japaihomais^dvija.uttamas^(c)//{BṣPṣ śudrau}{F śūdrau}{BṣPṣ japai}{F japais. }
body.translated_text: A <s>Vaiśya</s> and <s>Śūdra</s> through wealth, but the best of the twice-born through recitation and oblations.
Just as horses without a chariot, or a chariot without horses [would be useless],
So is austerity for one without knowledge, or knowledge for one without austerity.
Just as food combined with honey, or honey combined with food [is excellent],
So austerity and knowledge combined are the great medicine.
A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> endowed with knowledge and austerity, devoted to daily recitation,
Even one who always commits sinful deeds is not bound by sin.
Is not bound by sin—thus.
Even if a hundred sinful deeds and more have been committed, if the <s>Veda</s> is retained,
The fire of the <s>Veda</s> burns all that away, as fire [burns] fuel.
Just as fire, when grown strong, burns even moist trees,
So the fire of the <s>Veda</s> burns the fault born of [past] action.

body.text: Va.27.3 hatvā(han-)^api sa imān lokān bhuñjānas(bhuj-)^api yatas tatas^(c)/
body.translated_text: Even though he has killed, even though he enjoys [the fruits] from here and there,
A learned <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who retains the <s>Ṛg Veda</s> incurs no sin whatsoever.
One should not, relying on the power of the <s>Veda</s>, take delight in sinful actions;

body.text: Va.27.4 a.jñānāt^ca pramādāt^ca dahyate(dah-) karma na^itarat (c)//
body.translated_text: From ignorance and from heedlessness, [only past] <s>karma</s> is burned, not the other [i.e., deliberate sin].
A sage who performs austerity in the forest, subsisting on roots and fruits,

body.text: Va.27.5 ṛcam ekām^ca yas^adhīte(adhi-i-) tat^ca tāni ca tat samam (c)//
body.translated_text: And one who studies even a single <s>ṛc</s> (verse)—that [study] and those [austerities] are equal.
One should supplement the <s>Veda</s> with the <s>Itihāsas</s> and <s>Purāṇas</s>;
The <s>Veda</s> fears the one of scant learning: 'This one will strike me.'
Daily practice of the <s>Veda</s> according to one's ability, and the regular performance of the great sacrifices (<s>mahāyajñas</s>),
Quickly destroy sins, even those born of great transgressions (<s>mahāpātaka</s>).
One should tirelessly perform one's own duty as declared by the <s>Veda</s>;

body.text: Va.27.8 tat^hi kurvan(kṛ-) yathāśaktyā prāpnoti(pra-āp-) paramām^gatim (c)//
body.translated_text: For one who performs it to the best of his ability attains the highest goal.
From sacrificing [for others], from teaching, from [accepting gifts due to] kinship, and likewise from accepting gifts from improper persons,
No fault accrues to <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, for he is like fire and the sun.
When a situation of doubt arises, known as [involving] what is unfit and what is fit to eat,
I shall declare the purification of food—listen to me as I speak.
One should drink, without alkali or salt, the rough [plant] <s>Brāhmī</s> (Bacopa), <s>Suvarcalā</s>,
And <s>Śaṅkhapuṣpī</s>, with milk, for three nights—a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [is thus purified].
Having boiled <s>Palāśa</s> leaves, <s>Bilva</s> leaves, <s>Kuśa</s> grass, lotus, and <s>Udumbara</s> [fig tree parts],
One should drink the water; one is purified within three nights.
Cow's urine, cow dung, milk, curds, ghee, and water infused with <s>Kuśa</s> grass,
Together with a one-night fast—this would purify even a <s>Śvapāka</s> (outcaste).
Cow's urine, cow dung, milk, curds, and ghee—
One who subsists on these for five nights is purified by <s>Pañcagavya</s> (the five products of the cow).
One who consumes barley according to the prescribed method is purified in a manifest way;
When there is purity of disposition, they are pure; but when impure, they remain stained.

body.text: Va.27.16 haviṣyān prātar āśān^trīn sāyam āśān^tathā^eva ca (c)/
body.translated_text: Three meals of <s>haviṣya</s> (sacrificial food) in the morning, and likewise three meals in the evening,
And [three meals] unsolicited—there should be three fasts [as well].
Now, if one wishes to perform it quickly: one day subsisting on air,

body.text: Va.27.17 rātrau jala.āśaye vyuṣṭas^prājāpatyena tat samam (c)//
body.translated_text: Spending the night in water, [and rising at dawn]—this is equal to the <s>Prājāpatya</s> [penance].
Having recited the <s>Sāvitrī</s> (<s>Gāyatrī</s> mantra) eight thousand times at sunrise,

body.text: Va.27.18 mucyate(muc-) pātakais^sarvais^yadi na brahma.hā bhavet(bhū-) (c)//
body.translated_text: One is freed from all sins, provided one is not a slayer of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.
He who is a thief, a drinker of liquor, a destroyer of embryos, or one who has violated the teacher's bed—
Having studied the <s>Dharmaśāstra</s>, he is freed from all sins.
For ill-fated deeds, for badly performed [rites], and for great sins,
The <s>Kṛcchra</s> penance and the <s>Cāndrāyaṇa</s> [penance] are the destroyers of all sin.

body.text: Va.27.21 ekaikam^vardhayet(vṛdh-) piṇḍam^śukle kṛṣṇe ca hrāsayet(hras-) (c)/
body.translated_text: One should increase [the food] by one morsel [each day] during the bright [fortnight], and decrease [it] during the dark [fortnight];
On the new-moon day, one should not eat—this is the rule of the <s>Cāndrāyaṇa</s> [penance].
This is the rule of the <s>Cāndrāyaṇa</s>—thus.

body.text: Va.28.1 na strī duṣyati(duṣ-) jāreṇa na vipras^veda.karmaṇā (c)/
body.translated_text: A woman is not defiled by a paramour, nor a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> by Vedic rites,
Nor water by urine and excrement, nor fire by the act of burning.

body.text: Va.28.2 svayam^vipratipannā vā yadi vā vipravāsitā (c)/
body.translated_text: Whether she herself has gone astray, or has been banished,

body.text: Va.28.2 balāt kāra.upabhuktā vā cora.hasta.gatā^api vā (c)//
body.translated_text: Or enjoyed by force, or fallen into the hands of a thief—

body.text: Va.28.3 na tyājyā(tyaj-) dūṣitā nārī na^asyās tyāgas^vidhīyate(vi-dhā-) (c)/
body.translated_text: A defiled woman should not be abandoned; her abandonment is not prescribed.
One should wait for her menstrual period; she is purified by the time of her menses.
The purification of women is incomparable; they are never defiled,
For their monthly flow removes their misdeeds each month.
Women were formerly enjoyed by the gods—by <s>Soma</s>, <s>Gandharva</s>, and <s>Agni</s>;

body.text: Va.28.5 gacchanti(gam-) mānuṣān paścānaitā duṣyanti(duṣ-) dharmatas^(c)//{BṣPṣ paścānaitā}{F paścāt. na. etās.}
body.translated_text: They come to human men afterward; they are not defiled according to <s>dharma</s>.
<s>Soma</s> gave them purity, <s>Gandharva</s> gave them refined speech,
And <s>Agni</s> gave them complete sanctity—therefore women are without blemish.

body.text: Va.28.7 trīṇi striyas^pātakāni loke dharma.vidas^vidus(vid-)^(c)/{BṣPṣ striyas}{F striyās}
body.translated_text: Three transgressions of women are known to the knowers of <s>dharma</s> in this world:
The murder of the husband, the killing of an embryo, and the abortion of one's own fetus.
A calf is pure at the udder [i.e., when suckling]; a bird [is pure] when it causes a fruit to fall;

body.text: Va.28.8 striyas^ca rati.saṃsarge śvā mṛga.grahaṇe śucis^(c)//
body.translated_text: Women are [pure] in the act of love-making; a dog is pure in catching prey.

body.text: Va.28.9 aja.aśvās^mukhatas^medhyās gāvas^medhyās tu sarvatas^(c)//[Bhler seems to read: gāvo medhyāś ca pṛṣṭhataḥ, also cf. ḍevala ṝuoted in KK. śuddhi-kāṇḍa p.176:1]
body.translated_text: Goats and horses are pure from the mouth; cows are pure from everywhere.
I shall henceforth declare all the Vedic purifiers,

body.text: Va.28.10 yeṣām^japais^ca homais^ca pūyante(pū-) na^atra saṃśayas^(c)//
body.translated_text: By the recitation and oblation of which one is purified—there is no doubt about this.
The <s>Aghamarṣaṇa</s> [hymn], the <s>Devakṛta</s>, the <s>Śuddhavatīs</s>, the <s>Taratsamā</s> [verses],
The <s>Kūṣmāṇḍas</s>, the <s>Pāvamānīs</s>, the <s>Durgā</s>-<s>Sāvitrī</s>,
The <s>Atīṣaṅga</s> [hymns], the <s>Padastobha</s> [chants], the <s>Sāmans</s>, and the <s>Vyāhṛtis</s>,
The <s>Bhāruṇḍa</s> <s>Sāmans</s>, the <s>Gāyatra</s> [<s>Sāman</s>], and the <s>Raivata</s> [<s>Sāman</s>],

body.text: Va.28.13 puruṣa.vratam^ca bhāsam^ca tathā deva.vratāni ca (c)/
body.translated_text: The <s>Puruṣavrata</s> and the <s>Bhāsa</s>, and the <s>Devavrata</s> [hymns],
The <s>Abliṅga</s>, the <s>Bārhaspatya</s>, the <s>Vāksūkta</s>, and the <s>Madhṛcas</s> (honey-verses),
The <s>Śatarudriya</s>, the <s>Atharvaśiras</s>, the <s>Trisuparṇa</s>, the <s>Mahāvrata</s>,
The <s>Gosūkta</s> (hymn to cows), the <s>Aśvasūkta</s> (hymn to horses), and the two <s>Sāmans</s> on the Pure and Impure.
The three <s>Ājyadohas</s>, the <s>Rathantara</s>, the Vow of <s>Agni</s>, the <s>Vāmadevya</s>, and the <s>Bṛhat</s>—

body.text: Va.28.15 etāni japtāni punanti(pū-) jantūnjāti.smaratvam^labhate(labh-) yadi^icchet(iṣ-) (c)//
body.translated_text: These, when recited, purify beings; and if one wishes, one obtains the recollection of [past] births.
Gold is the offspring of <s>Agni</s>; the earth belongs to <s>Viṣṇu</s>; and cows are the daughters of the Sun;

body.text: Va.28.16 tāsām anantam^phalam aśnuvīta(aś-) yas^kān.canam^gām^ca mahīm^ca dadyāt(dā-) (c)//
body.translated_text: He who gives gold, a cow, and land obtains their infinite fruit.
A cow, a horse, gold, and land obstruct [i.e., turn away from] the giver
When they see the hand of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who is not learned in the <s>Vedas</s> and who has been rejected.

body.text: Va.28.18 vaiśākhyām^paurṇamāsyām^tu brāhmaṇān sapta pañca vā (c)/
body.translated_text: On the full-moon day of <s>Vaiśākha</s>, to five or seven <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>,

body.text: Va.28.18 tilān kṣaudreṇa saṃyuktān kṛṣṇān vā yadi vā^itarān (c)//
body.translated_text: Sesame seeds mixed with honey, whether black or otherwise—
[Saying] 'May the King of <s>Dharma</s> (<s>Yama</s>) be pleased,' or whatever arises in the mind—
The sin committed over an entire lifetime is destroyed at that very moment.
Having fashioned [an image of a bull] with a golden navel, with hooves, made of black [sesame] goat [hide],
He who gives [it] covered with sesame seeds—hear the meritorious fruit of that:
The earth, with its gold-filled caves, with its mountains, forests, and groves,

body.text: Va.28.21 catus.vaktrā bhavet(bhū-)^dattā pṛthivī na^atra saṃśayas^(c)//
body.translated_text: With its four faces [i.e., in all directions]—that [earth] is given [to him]; there is no doubt.
Placing sesame seeds on a black antelope skin, along with gold, honey, and ghee—

body.text: Va.28.22 dadāti(dā-) yas tu viprāya sarvam^tarati(tṛ-) duṣkṛtām(c) iti //
body.translated_text: He who gives [this] to a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> crosses over all evil. Thus.
Crosses over all evil—thus.
Through giving, one obtains all desires.
A celibate student [attains] long life and beauty.
One who practices non-violence is reborn in heaven.
From entering fire, [one attains] the world of <s>Brahman</s>.
From silence, good fortune.
From dwelling in water, [one becomes] lord of the <s>Nāgas</s> (serpents).
Free from disease, with depleted treasury [i.e., having given away all wealth].
A giver of water [attains] the fulfillment of all desires.
A giver of food [attains] good eyesight and [strong] memory.
Intelligent [becomes] the giver of fearlessness to all.
From [gifts associated with] the cow-yoke, [one attains the merit of] bathing at all sacred fords.
From the gift of a bed and seat, sovereignty of the inner apartments [i.e., kingship].
From the gift of an umbrella, the attainment of a house.
A giver of a house obtains a city.

body.text: Va.29.15 upānat.pradātā yanam āsādayate(ā-sad-) //{BṣPṣ yanam}{E yānam}
body.translated_text: A giver of sandals obtains a vehicle.
Moreover, they cite [the following]:
Whatever sin a man commits, pressed by [the need for] livelihood,
He is purified even by the gift of land the size of a cow's hide.
One should give a full water vessel (<s>kamaṇḍalu</s>) to a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> for the purpose of sipping water (<s>ācamana</s>);
After death, having attained supreme satisfaction, one is born again as a drinker of <s>Soma</s>.
Thousands of oxen given, [those that are] yoke-bearing and load-carrying—
A gift properly given to a worthy recipient is equal to the gift of a maiden.
Three [gifts] they call supreme gifts: cows, the earth, and <s>Sarasvatī</s> (learning);
A supreme gift among gifts, but the gift of knowledge is even greater.
Producing the fruit of finality, liberating from the cycle of <s>saṃsāra</s>—
He who, learned and free from envy, follows this conduct—
Faithful, pure, and self-controlled—whether he recites [it] or hears [it],

body.text: Va.29.21 vihāya(vi-hā-) sarva.pāpāni nāka.pṛṣṭhe mahīyate(mah-).(c) iti //
body.translated_text: Having abandoned all sins, he is glorified on the vault of heaven. Thus.
Is glorified on the vault of heaven—thus.
Practice <s>dharma</s>, not <s>adharma</s>; speak the truth, not falsehood;
Look far, not near; look to the highest, not to the lowest.
A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is fire.
Fire indeed is a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>—so says the <s>śruti</s>.
And how is that?

body.text: Va.30.5 tatra sadas^brāhmaṇasya śarīram^vedis^saṃkalpas^yajñas^paśus^ātmā raśanā buddhis^sadas^mukham āhavanīyam^nābhyām udaras^agnis^gārhapatyas^prāṇas^adhvaryus^apānas^hotā vyānas^brahmā samānas^udgātā^ātmā^indriyāṇi yajña.pātrāṇi yas^evam^vidvān(vid-) indriyais^indriya.artham^juhoti(hu-)^iti^api ca -- kāṭhake vijñāyate(vi-jñā-) //
body.translated_text: Va.30.5 There, the body of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is the sacrificial hall (<s>sadas</s>); the altar is [his] resolve; the sacrifice is [his] self (<s>ātman</s>); the animal [to be sacrificed] is [his] restraint (<s>raśanā</s>); the intellect is the hall; the mouth is the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire; the navel and belly are the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire; the <s>prāṇa</s> (outbreath) is the <s>Adhvaryu</s> priest; the <s>apāna</s> (inbreath) is the <s>Hotṛ</s> priest; the <s>vyāna</s> (diffused breath) is the <s>Brahmā</s> priest; the <s>samāna</s> (equalizing breath) is the <s>Udgātṛ</s> priest; the self is [the sacrificer]; the senses are the sacrificial implements. 'He who, knowing this, offers the sense-objects through the senses'—this too is known in the <s>Kāṭhaka</s> [<s>Saṃhitā</s>].
Va.30.6 And they also cite [the following]:

body.text: Va.30.6 pāti(pā-) trāti(tṛ-) ca dātāram ātmānam^ca^eva kilbiṣāt (c)/
body.translated_text: Va.30.6 [The offering] protects and saves the giver, and [saves] oneself too from sin,
Va.30.6 when offered into the fires of the mouths of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> that are enriched with the fuel of the <s>Vedas</s>.

body.text: Va.30.7 na skandate(skand-) na vyathate(vyath-) na^enam adhyāpatet(adhi-ā-pat-)^ca yat (c)/
body.translated_text: Va.30.7 It does not spill, it does not waver, and nothing falls upon it—

body.text: Va.30.7 variṣṭham agni.hotrāt tu brāhmaṇasya mukhe hutam (c)//
body.translated_text: Va.30.7 the offering made in the mouth of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is superior to the <s>Agnihotra</s>.
Va.30.8 Meditation is the fire; truth is the heaping of fuel; forbearance is the oblation; modesty (<s>hrī</s>) is the ladle; the offering-cake (<s>puroḍāśa</s>) is non-violence; contentment

body.text: Va.30.8 yūpas^kṛcchram^bhūtebhyas^abhaya.dākṣiṇyam iti kṛtvā(kṛ-) kratu mānasam^yāti(yā-) kṣayam^budhas^(c)//
body.translated_text: Va.30.8 is the sacrificial post; [the act of] giving fearlessness and kindness to all beings is the sacrificial fee (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>)—having thus performed the mental sacrifice (<s>mānasa kratu</s>), the wise one goes to the imperishable [realm].
Va.30.9 The hair decays of one who is decaying; the teeth decay of one who is decaying;

body.text: Va.30.9 jīvana.āśā dhana.āśā ca jīryatas(jṝ-)^api na jīryati(jṝ-) (c)//
body.translated_text: Va.30.9 but the desire for life and the desire for wealth do not decay even in one who is decaying.

body.text: Va.30.10 yā dus.tyajā dus.matibhis^yā na jīryati(jṝ-) jīryatas(jṝ-)^(c)/
body.translated_text: Va.30.10 That which is hard to abandon for those of foolish mind, that which does not decay even when one is decaying,
Va.30.10 that which is a disease [lasting] until the end of life—happiness [comes] to one who abandons that craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>). Thus it is said.

body.text: Va.30.11 namas^astu(as-) mitrāvaruṇayos^urvaśī.ātmajāya śatayātave vasiṣṭhāya vasiṣṭhāya^iti //
body.translated_text: Va.30.11 Salutation to <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>! To <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, the son of <s>Urvaśī</s>, who goes a hundred ways—to <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>!
End of the Text.
